52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.name: Lithographs after the panoramic photograph taken by Robertson and Beato, *Faust: Poligrafisch Illustrirte*, Zeitschrift, 1857, Vienna
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.keywords: Istanbul panorama; Faust; tower of War Ministry in Beyazıt
52eaca9c-9b61-57ba-8d7c-426a9c33c3f1.description2: James Robertson is the first Istanbul photographer known to have taken 360 degree panoramic photographs of the city. The first panorama, which was taken in May 1854 from the War Ministry tower in Beyazıt, consists of twelve separate photographs. The most successful printed reproductions based on Robertson’s photographs curiously enough were produced in Vienna. Issues of *Faust* published during 1857 report fascinating bits of information as well as pictures that are important to the history of printing and visual arts in the Ottoman Empire. A plate published in *Faust* contained a panoramic view from the Istanbul Beyazıt tower that is made from Robertson’s panorama.

5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.name: *Illustrated dictionary of Tunisia: the people and things of Tunisia*
5384029c-eb52-5179-984d-a80e0e272e8c.description2: Italian immigration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. This is evident from advertisements such as this one, where the headquarters, names and addresses of a Tunis-based firm are Italian.

53ec6f4f-bd40-5ba2-8874-cb460c22b748.name: Privateer ship flags
53ec6f4f-bd40-5ba2-8874-cb460c22b748.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
53ec6f4f-bd40-5ba2-8874-cb460c22b748.author: Bechir Yazidi
53ec6f4f-bd40-5ba2-8874-cb460c22b748.description2: This flag is divided into three sections, arranged in parallel along a long mast. The topmost flag has a red stripe and a black stripe, the middle is in the same shade of red, with three gold crescents in the centre, and the final flag is also red with a sword resembling that of the Prophet's cousin and fourth caliph, 'Ali.

55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.name: A map of Tunisia (1:1,600,000) showing Italian agricultural settlements, mines, coral- and sponge-fishing areas and boat lines
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.author: Giulia Barrera
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.third_name: Carta della Tunisia protettorato francese, 1906 disegnata dal prof Cesidio Bonanni
55244670-bd54-51f4-982e-13682dbb1443.description2: The green rectangles on the map indicate Italian agricultural settlements; the number of settlers is indicated as well. In 1906 the majority of the Italian peasants had settled around Tunis and the Gulf of Hammamet. By contrast, few Italian peasants had settled in the South and in the interior of the country (the map indicated only 300 Italian peasants near Sfax and 400 near Kef).

5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.name: Four guns
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms; armour; Gun
5747fe8d-4ab0-565c-9e90-6e797f311e64.description2: These Turkish flintlock pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They have a wooden butt stock, a slightly broken wooden forend and a round barrel. They are made of wood and cast steel.

578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.name: Palais du Bardo
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.keywords: Palais du Bardo; beylical throne; European influences; Italian influences
578a0774-be4c-5eb0-85a3-86bf64c69e71.description2: This postcard shows the throne room of the Palais du Bardo, with its rich furnishings and monumental chandeliers hanging from the ceiling. The bey's throne sits in the centre, surrounded by paintings of the princes of the Husainid dynasty, painted wooden ceilings, mirrors and console tables carved and painted with gold leaf, and with two great rooms on either side. From the 18th century onwards the Husainid beys continuously expanded and decorated the Palais du Bardo. The architecture and furniture all indicate a strong European, particularly Italian, influence.

58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.name: Dr Charles Nicolle, Nobel Laureate for Medicine
58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
58837723-b1a0-5787-a2b8-812f79e409c5.description2: This is a photograph of Dr Charles Nicolle carrying out child vaccination on the indigenous Tunisian population. During his time at l'Institut Pasteur (1903–1936) he worked to prevent or eradicate infectious illnesses

58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.name: *Vue d'Alger*
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.author: Dalila Orfali
58b9f9f7-6b17-532d-8f51-0f4b19d4fb8d.description2: These two original lithographs depict the city of al-Jaza'ir (Algiers) prior to the English bombardment led by Lord Exmouth on 26 August 1816. The regency was ruled first by the *Beylerbeys* (general governors) from 1518 to 1587, then by the Pashas from 1587 to 1659, the *Aghas* from 1659 to 1671 and the Deys from 1671 to 1830. The reign of the final Dey of Algiers, Hussein, lasted 12 years until the French conquest in 1830.

59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.name: *The political refugee*
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.second_name: Illustration for "The Bohemians of Paris", *Le Charivari* 11
59043927-aae8-5c23-9db7-2ff253833d51.description2: The cartoonist Honoré Daumier (1808–1879) was one of the first to be interested in the theme of migration, and drew many cartoon strips which dealt with the difficulties of exile. He did some more comic drawings on this theme, which are harder to understand. In this image, published in a series on the theme of the "Bohemian" (an artistic community attempting to live without restrictions), he highlights the gaze of his contemporaries on the "other" or the "stranger". The image also mocks the suspicious young woman just as much as the asylum seeker.

5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.name: Pair of pistols
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms and armour; Pistol; Coral; Silver
5b229743-fc47-5975-b220-b56bbbada7be.description2: These Turkish flintlock pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They have a wooden bulbous butt plate and engraved silver mounts ornamented with coral. They are made of wood and cast steel and have a small, ornamental, engraved silver piece on the wooden grip.

5c13cdb4-c7e6-5dcb-af04-c009378b92a9.name: List of 49 men, women and children from the district of Chiavari (on the Italian cost, near Genoa) who were kept as slaves in Tunis, Tripoli and Algiers, in March 1816
5c13cdb4-c7e6-5dcb-af04-c009378b92a9.author: Alfonso Assini
5c13cdb4-c7e6-5dcb-af04-c009378b92a9.archival: ASGe, Magistrato per il riscatto degli schiavi, 129, doc. 17
5c13cdb4-c7e6-5dcb-af04-c009378b92a9.description2: In 1771, Tunisian corsairs had kidnapped in this very district Gian Battista Raffo, a watchmaker who later fathered Giuseppe Raffo (1795-1862) who in turn served for several years as Tunisian Foreign Affairs Minister.

en: Clancy-Smith, Julia, *Mediterraneans: North Africa and Europe in an Age of Migration, c. 1800–1900*, Oakland, CA: University of California Press, 2011.

5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.name: Maronite Benevolent Catholic Society of New York rule book
5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
5cdd4963-ab03-5834-84db-f850572ca208.description2: A copy of the book of regulations for the Maronite Benevolent Catholic Society of New York, a charitable society aimed at helping the needy within the Maronite community. It provided financial support for the poor and free medication for the sick, and financially supported burial of the deceased. The book outlines the objectives, rules and structure of the association.

5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.name: An open letter from the Tuscan community in Constantinople to the Chargé d’Affairs of Tuscany, protesting the detention of three Italian democrats exiled by Ottoman authorities
5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.author: Massimo Sanacore
5d280899-351f-5ef7-95bb-ed98a12d141d.description2: Italian communities abroad actively supported the movement for Italian national unification known as “Risorgimento”. The Italian community in Constantinople raised funding to donate a cannon to the Kingdom of Sardinia, which in 1848 was at war with the Austrian Empire. After the Kingdom of Sardinia’s army was defeated, conflicts between the most moderate wing of the nationalist movement and the republicans (supporters of Giuseppe Mazzini) broke out and the Kingdom of Sardinia’s authorities started to persecute the latter.

5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.name: *Family gathering in Alexandria*
5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.author: Maria Dimitriadou
5e9e845e-5f4e-508c-91ed-f52d967dbf97.description2: Black and white photo in a family album: A family gathering at the garden of Emmanuel Benaki’s mansion in Alexandria. His eldest daughter Alexandra Benaki was engaged to his partner Tom Davis in April 1889. In the center of the picture appear the bride and the groom, the sister of Alexandra Benaki, Penelope Benaki-Delta, as well as their mother, Virginia Benaki. Phototographer unknown.

5eedbbb5-d4fb-57a8-ae2f-5c2682f16249.name: Document regarding slavery and piracy
5eedbbb5-d4fb-57a8-ae2f-5c2682f16249.holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
5eedbbb5-d4fb-57a8-ae2f-5c2682f16249.author: Bechir Yazidi
5eedbbb5-d4fb-57a8-ae2f-5c2682f16249.keywords: Ahmed Pacha Bey; abolition of slavery
5eedbbb5-d4fb-57a8-ae2f-5c2682f16249.description2: This document is written in Arabic on two sheets of parchment. The page on the right dates to 1842 and contains Ahmed Pacha Bey's correspondence regarding the end of the slave markets, whilst the page on the left dates to 1846 and deals with the abolition of the slave trade.  Length: 30 cm. Width: 40 cm.

63191935-a807-58a4-b11e-292c88a654f7.name: Dawud Pasha’s living room
63191935-a807-58a4-b11e-292c88a654f7.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
63191935-a807-58a4-b11e-292c88a654f7.description2: This bedroom belonged to the first *mutasarrif* (ruler) of the Mount Lebanon *mutasarrifiyya*, Dawud Pasha, who governed from 1861–68). The room is furnished with four armchairs and one large sofa. The sofa has a high wooden back, covered with a mosaic of white, beige and brown ceramic and bone pieces, organised in floral and geometric patterns. The seat cushions are covered with navy and beige silk decorated with similar patterns. The sofa was reserved for guests, which Dawud Pasha would receive from his large armchair, a sign of power and authority. The room is lit by two glass lanterns painted with white and golden floral patterns, and a round copper table sits in the centre of the room.

6345c672-a66e-5ec9-a903-e3ddfbdcb159.name: *Chiefs of nomadic Arab tribes in Syria visit the Abbot Desmazure, Latin father of the Saint-Sépulcre in the Convent of the Latin Fathers of Jerusalem, built on mount Gihon*
6345c672-a66e-5ec9-a903-e3ddfbdcb159.description2: Syrian tribal leaders visited the Abbot Desmazure in 1827, in the Convent of the Latin Fathers of Jerusalem. He happily volunteered to show Jerusalem to visitors passing through the city, and tried hard to find diplomatic solutions to the religious tensions within the Christian community.

640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.name: Municipal theatre
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.history: This building, which was once the Municipal Casino and often affectionately known as the "bonbonnière Resplandy", was built in the early 20th century in the Art Nouveau style by the French Architect Jean-Émile Resplandy and located on Avenue Jules-Ferry (now Avenue Habib-Bourguiba) in the heart of the European quarter. It has been constantly active since its birth, clearing the way for new artistic talent. The biggest names in Tunisian and Arab performing arts stood on its stage, performing ballet, opera, dramatic performances, classical concerts and more. In 2011 it became an important symbol of the Tunisian revolution; protestors, martyrs and rebels from all sides stood on its steps at some point.
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.keywords: Art Nouveau; theatre; stucco; bas reliefs; Apollo
640cbdc1-fd31-5fad-89d3-4deff3b9943f.description2: This theatre, the last remnant of a municipal artistic complex, can hold up to 1,350 seats. An immense white building, it reflects the style of Art Nouveau with evidence for some baroque influences. The bas-relief decorations, showing a scene with Apollo and the two muses, dominate the façade. The interior, from the vestibule to foyer, is notable for its modern structure and the richness of the carved stucco decorations. The bas-reliefs, moulds, cornices and balconies were all made by famous French and Italian artists.

661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.name: Railway station
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.history: The establishment of the French Protectorate in Tunisia (12 May 1881) quickly led to the introduction of a railway network throughout the country, to support civilian control in the areas where the Europeans had settled. The Grombalia station is an example of one of the new public buildings. This region has always occupied an important strategic position on the communication routes from North to South Tunisia, and its temperate climate and fertile lands made it home to an important wine-producing centre and European settlement, particularly for the Italians and the French.
661636db-2ce1-5462-80af-0f6986d618f3.description2: Designed by the French government during the colonial era as a building for public use, the Grombalia rail station is a rectangular building of around 100 m2 with no architectural features of note. The station is on the ground floor, which contains a shop, ticket office, and waiting room. The first floor was used for the stationmaster's accommodation. Its double-sloped roof is covered in red tiles, and the blue painting around the large windows are juxtaposed with the white façade. The Grombalia station is still in use today.

6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.name: Italian and Tunisian miners at work
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.author: Giulia Barrera
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 27
6810a977-0fac-5c5e-a9a2-56e6c3bc3a3a.description2: According to the book where this photo was published, in 1906 the largest number of Italian miners in Tunisia worked in El Kef (2,000) and in Gafsa (1,200). The most important mineral resource in Tunisia were phosphates, but the country also had mines of copper, manganese, iron and lead. One could find Italian miners in all these mines.

69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.name: Colonial style building
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian *palazzo*) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
69063980-1b98-599a-87aa-a06e11b7637c.description2:
These two residential buildings at 40 and 42 Rue Oum-Kalthoum are two remarkable examples of the Art Nouveau architecture, built between 1906 and 1908. The façades are decorated with a beautiful pattern of cherubs, ribbons, small female heads and garlands, all organised with symmetrically.  
  
The Azerm Building at 53 Avenue de Carthage, built between 1905 and 1906, is a private residence. It is notable for its curved lines, balconies with irregular arches and walled niches. The abundance of rich decorations are evidence of the craftsmen's excellent skill. These buildings are perfect examples of the rich decorations of neo-baroque architecture, the huge curls of Art Nouveau, and the abundance of rococo architecture.

690dbb87-8510-5df7-8b14-e1bf920ecdbc.name: Turkish council seats
690dbb87-8510-5df7-8b14-e1bf920ecdbc.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
690dbb87-8510-5df7-8b14-e1bf920ecdbc.description2: Seats such as these were used to furnish Ottoman councils. They are made of thin mattresses (c. 5cm thick) covered in thick, dark coloured fabric, usually in navy, burgundy or beige.

6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.name: Third-grade pupils of the Italian state-funded Giovanni Meli primary school in Tunis
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.author: Giulia Barrera
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 107
6996faf2-9ef0-57f8-8ffd-b45d86af0d67.description2:
In 1831, siblings Pompeo and Ester Sulema, political refugees from Livorno, opened the first Italian school in Tunis. By the end of the 19th century, there were 21 Italian state schools in Tunisia: 13 in Tunis, three in La Goulette, three in Sousse and two in Sfax. Five of them were pre-schools, eleven were primary schools and five were secondary schools.  
The Italian State could run schools in Tunisia thanks to the treaty signed by Italy and Tunisia in 1868. In 1881, Tunisia became a French protectorate and in 1896 Italy and France signed a treaty over the status of Italians in Tunisia: the Italian state could continue to run schools in Tunisia but could not open new ones. So, classes became very crowded, as shown in this photo.

en: Pendola, M., *Gli italiani di Tunisia: storia di una comunità (XIX-XX secolo)*, Foligno: Editoriale Umbra, 2007.

69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.name: Marius Scalesi
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.holder: Institut Culturel Italien (Italian Emabassy in Tunisia)
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.keywords: Marius Scalesi; literature in French; poetry; migration
69f1c95c-2875-58ff-b85b-10d1c2d2ab83.description2: Pictured here is Marius (Mario) Scalesi, a young poet of Italian origin, born on 6 February 1892 in Tunis to an Italian father and a Maltese mother. He suffered from tuberculosis from birth, and became paralysed following a fall down the stairs in his home in La Goulette, the so-called "Little Sicily" of Tunis. Forced to abandon his studies in order to make a living, he completed his education independently. His articles of literary criticism and poems were published in the journal *La Tunisie Illustrée*. His collection of poems, *Les Poèmes d'un Maudit* sheds light on the hardships of his life. He died in 1922 in an asylum in Palermo. A fascinating figure due to his triple cultural identity - Italian, French and Tunisian - he is considered one of the pioneers of North African poetry in French.

6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.name: The Bach Hamba brothers
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.author: Bechir Yazidi
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.keywords: Newspaper Le Tunisien; the Young Tunisians movement
6a3c68eb-7bea-5e92-8112-9d9d0c950351.description2: 'Ali (pictured here) and Mohamed were two of the leaders of the protest movement "Harakat al-Shabab al-Tunisi" (the Young Tunisians). Born in Tunis in 1876 and 1881 respectively, these two men of Turkish origin helped found a French-language newspaper, *Le Tunisien*, through which they attacked the politics of the French colonialists and demanded reform. With the help of their comrades, the brothers organised many acts of resistance, such as the Jellaz Affair (1911) and the tramway boycott (1912). The arrest of the majority of the movement's founders, and the suppression of the newspaper *Le Tunisien* marked the end of their activities in Tunisia. However, they continued to make their demands from abroad, working mainly in Geneva and Istanbul, where they finally died in 1818 ('Ali) and 1820 (Mohamed).

6c3d3ee7-fba0-54ef-ae3a-b0810a3caeb2.name: A bedouin and his camel/dromedary
6c3d3ee7-fba0-54ef-ae3a-b0810a3caeb2.description2: The bedouin became a symbol of romantic nomadism in the 19th century European imagination. The Zangaki brothers, a pair of Greek photographers working in Egypt, began producing photos of these nomads for Western tourists.

6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.name: Dinar
6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.description: Gold Dinar of Hijaz, King Hussein bin 'Ali, AH 1334. On November, 1916 the notables, ulama of Hijaz and a majority of the sheiks of Bedouins and sedentary tribes, assembled at the great Mosque of Mecca to pay allegiance to al-Hussein and proclaim him “King“ of Arab Countries. On this occasion a coin bearing his name at Mecca, as King of the Arabs was struck. But Britain, France and Italy recognized him only as “King of the Hijaz” on 3 January 1917. On obverse: "*bi-l-bilad al-'arabiyya al-husayn bin 'ali / 'abduhu / hashimi / wa ibn 'abdihi / al-nahidh*" ("Hussein bin Ali / God’s Servant / Hashimi /and son of God’s Servant / leader of Arab renaissance"). On reverse: "*duriba bi-makka al-mukarrama / sana 1334 / dinar / sana 8 / 'asima al-hukuma al-'arabiyya*" ("Dinar minted at Makka al-Mukarrama in 1334 \[AH\] in the reign year 8 capital of Arab Government"). All regular coins of Hijaz bear the accessional date of ١٣٣٤ (AH 1334) of al-Hussein bin 'Ali, plus the regional year, many bronze coins had a light silver wash.
6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.author: Aida Naghawi
6c5debca-9932-5c4a-89ab-f8f3d13de354.keywords: Hussein bin Ali; dinar; Arab Hashemite Government; Mecca al Mukarrama; coin; currency; coinage; numismatics

6d50fc9a-40d7-5903-b14d-ddd9bf5e5e84.name: Jacket
6d50fc9a-40d7-5903-b14d-ddd9bf5e5e84.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
6d50fc9a-40d7-5903-b14d-ddd9bf5e5e84.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's military uniform. It is made of red velvet and embroidered with a yellow gilded thread.

6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.name: Stucco panel
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.keywords: Carved plaster; capitals; palaces; Ottoman style; Italian-esque style
6db232a1-1948-537d-8bad-3c92a264c7c0.description2: "Stucco" is a term used to describe the vast majority of decorations in Islamic Arts. White stucco, made from plaster stones, was used for column capitals, arcs, as well as sloped constructions such as roofs, as it is an incredibly supple, yet strong, adherent, durable and light material. Muslim artisans made countless constructions decorated with stucco. The 18th and 19th centuries, however, saw many constructions in carved golden plaster - both palaces and houses were elaborately decorated in this way. Floral motifs, closer to the Ottoman and Italian styles, soon overtook the geometric designs of previous centuries.

6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.name: *Tsar Nikolai II enters Paris, 6 October 1896*
6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.keywords: Diplomacy; France; Russia; Nicholas II; Paris
6f001e78-8dfc-56a6-bec2-b6b68344cfd8.description2: Tsar Nikolai II's visit to France in October 1896 was front page news. The French government, hoping to highlight the importance of this day, marked the occasion by giving students the day off, stopping all special train services, and meticulously preparing the path the imperial couple would take once arriving at Cherbourg Port. The true purpose of the trip was to preserve the precious Franco-Russian alliance signed in 1893 with Aleksandr III. Pictured in this image are the Tsar and his wife, accompanied by the President of the Republic Félix Faure, and greeted by a crowd of almost half a million on the Champs-Élysées. The popular imagery contributed to the success and immortalisation of the event.

6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.name: Organ Made in Tunis by the Italian Firm Cesare Trionfo and Exhibited in Milan
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.author: Giulia Barrera
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 197.
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.third_name: *Organo costruito a Tunisi dalla Ditta Cesare Trionfo ed esposto a Milano*
6faa2e57-f95c-52d9-a61f-402154b53322.description2:
Cesare Trionfo was a child when he migrated with his family to Tunisia from Livorno in 1855. He became a trader, and in 1886 he started trading musical instruments. In Tunis, he later also started a shop that made musical instruments such as this organ. Trionfo promoted the construction of the theatre Politeama Roissini, which he co-owned.  
This organ was exhibited in Milan for the 1906 international exhibition. The organ is a traditional Italian musical instrument. This one has decorative elements taken from Arab architecture.

70700c8a-84f5-533a-a08c-1e14bd325d9e.name: *The entrance of Zografeion Gymnasium in Istanbul*
70700c8a-84f5-533a-a08c-1e14bd325d9e.author: Maria Dimitriadou
70700c8a-84f5-533a-a08c-1e14bd325d9e.description2: A black and white photo from a leather bound album. It bepicts the *Zografion Gymnasion* in Constantinople. Photographer unknown.

70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.name: Clothing, sheets and blankets distributed by the Students’ Benevolent Fund to destitute Italian children in Tunis
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.author: Giulia Barrera
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 123
70c34b29-b413-5cf3-ba1c-bd2773093060.description2: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies to promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children by providing free books and clothes.

en: Pendola, M., *Gli italiani di Tunisia: storia di una comunità (XIX-XX secolo)*, Foligno: Editoriale Umbra, 2007.

712ff58d-128f-55d5-aad2-b4bc62cf22ab.name: *Le Petit Tunisien. Voice for French interests and communities in Tunisia.*
712ff58d-128f-55d5-aad2-b4bc62cf22ab.description2: Italian migration to Tunisia in the 19th century was, quantitively speaking, extremely significant. The French government had to bear in mind, however, that there remained significant population who had hoped Tunisia would become an Italian colony. Some French newspapers, such as *Le Petit Tunisien*, responded to this by emphasising their French-Italian links.

736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.name: *Mashrabiyya*
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
736574db-9cd1-5e72-95d5-f1860d3596ad.description2: The *mashrabiyya* is a decorative architectural element characteristic of residences in the Arab world. It was generally used on windows or balconies on the second floor or above. As well as being a natural ventilation device, the *mashrabiyya* served the purpose of shielding the occupant from the vision of passers' by, whilst still allowing natural light to pass through the gaps. This particular piece is square shaped and made of limestone, sculpted in floral patterns.

7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.name: *Khedive Ismail*
7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite
7445c306-1049-5630-9a00-27983ccbe9b6.description2: Khedive Ismail, the fifth ruler of the Muhammad 'Ali Dynasty, Khedive of Egypt from 1863 to 1879. Ismail assumed rule over Egypt when work on the Suez Canal was ongoing. He continued the project until the Canal was opened for navigation in 1869. He established Dar al-Kutub (the National Library and Archives of Egypt) on 26 September 1870. The First Egyptian Parliament was inaugurated in 1866, during his reign.

75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.name: Quran
75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.holder: Musée des Arts Islamiques de Kairouan
75ede8fe-76f3-5385-bdc5-f85fce889190.description2: These are two pages from a calligraphic Quran written in maghrebi script, dating to the 18th century, and a good example of the symbiosis between Hispano-Islamic and Ottoman influences. Although the script and the colour of the diacritics are typically maghrebi, the decoration and the frontispiece of the fatiha, which is adorned with floral motifs, shows the clear influence of the Ottoman school, which was itself inspired by Iranian art. The vowels are written in red, the *sukun* and the *shadda* in blue, the *hamza* in yellow or gold and the *hamza al-wasl* in green.

7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.name: The Promotional Exhibition of the Alsace and Lorraine Society in the Algerian Section [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.author: Marina Minozzi
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.archival: *L'Esposizione di Parigi del 1878 illustrata*, Sonzogno Editore, 1878, p. 88
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.keywords: Exposition universelle de Paris; industrialisation; exhibition building; Moorish city; exhibitions and urban spaces; Moorish style; Islamic architecture; reinterpretation; exoticism; reproduction; model; magazine; French architecture
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.copyright: Copyright image: Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Roma.
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.third_name: *La mostra della Società promotrice degli Alsaziani e Lorenesi nella Sezione Algerina*
7799c614-d39a-57bf-8c89-ac0c4d03ec70.description2: Paris, International Exhibition, 1878. In one of the streets in the Trocadero Pavilion buildings were constructed based on those built in Algeria after the French-Prussian war (1870–71) by the Society Protecting Alsatian and Lorenese People for refugees coming from France. The interior shows all the territories donated to the Protecting Society and in the lower part the villages of Hanssonvillers and Bacckhalfa.

77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.name: Colonial farms
77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.history: French colonialism brought significant changes to Tunisians' lifestyles, which consequently affected the country's rural architecture. The colonial settlers built their homes as soon as they arrived, and so Italian and French residential architecture evolved from a small hut to a large house. These old, often large, farmhouses punctuate the landscape with their red roofs and cellars, easily distinguishable against the green of the forest. They remind us that the great Italo-French rivalry was triggered by the competition over the best land, as viticulture was their main economic activity. Single-crop farming was used for these grapevines, which were almost entirely wine varieties.
77f5feea-8867-5c80-82a2-d05e34b6fff5.description2: This farmhouse, belonging to the French winemaker of Béja, can be distinguished by its white walls and industrial red tiles, stamped to show the name of their maker and place of origin. The tiles are overlapping to protect the house from the rainfall and snowfall. Contrary to the traditional farmhouses which were inward facing, this settler farmhouse has large windows on its façade and is built on a empty plot of land. The house is east facing and rectangular-based, with four annexes dedicated to the farm's needs, most importantly pressing the grapes and storing them in the cellars.

7821de49-1833-5656-935a-de7859fecc1b.name: Jacket
7821de49-1833-5656-935a-de7859fecc1b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
7821de49-1833-5656-935a-de7859fecc1b.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's jacket, probably worn during the winter months. It is made of dark blue wool, with floral patterns embroidered in black thread and bordered by a black ribbon. The lining is made of a mustard-coloured fabric.

79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.name: Marriage shawl
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.holder: Musée des Arts et Traditions Populaires
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
79fded3c-fc12-5fa3-bff4-6820a231b3e4.description2: This loose marriage shawl is decorated with various symbols of fertility. Two large rectangles of red wool are sewn together, and their joining seam is ornately decorated with gold embroidery. The decorations are spread out across the whole cloth, forming a strip of finely woven motifs in the centre, which is surrounded by various traditional figures and patterns. The human figures are characteristic of the (often enigmatic) decorative arts of the towns of El Jem and Ouerdanine, and feature here in addition to the more common motifs such as the fish, the hand, disks, circles, diamonds, crescents, the dove and the camel.

7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.name: Record of the marriage between the Egyptian governmental official Paul Draneht Bey, aged 55, and the Italian Adele Casati, aged 19, celebrated in Oggebbio (Italy) in 1873
7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.archival: AS VB, Comune di Oggebbio, Registro Atti di Matrimonio, vol. 523/24, firme degli sposi
7a673124-7bea-543e-8cdf-59c06cdc2216.description2: Apparently, Adelaide Casati and her sister Margarita attended the premiere of the Aida in Cairo (24 December 1871). Their father, Filippo, was participating in the performance as a cello player. In Cairo, the two Casati sisters met their future husbands, respectively, Paul Draneht, and the Greek banker, Joannis Sinadino (who acted as witness in the marriage between Paul Draneht and Adelaide Casati). Both men moved to live in Oggebbio, Italy, when Paul Draneht bought a villa there.

7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.name: Handwritten poem by Constantinos Kavafis
7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.author: Maria Dimitriadou
7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.keywords: poetry; Greek; Alexandria; Egypt; phanariote; Istanbul; Constantinople; Greek community; literature; journalism; migration; mithology; travel; exile; cosmopolitism; travel and exile in literature; mithology in literature; historical events in literature
7a8205d2-2d3a-59d3-b4bb-d33dce902734.description2: The poem *The City*, here labelled *Again at the same city* (*Pali stin idia poli*) handwritten by Constantinos Kavafis and dated August

7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.name: Treaty of Bardo
7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.author: Bechir Yazidi
7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.keywords: French protectorate of Tunisia; Sadok Pacha Bey
7c87bedb-5773-5c25-8dc4-6634c1e81d26.description2: Also known as the Treaty of Ksar Said, the Treaty of Bardo was signed by the Bey of Tunis and the French government on 12 May 1881. It consisted of two articles which established the French protectorate of Tunisia. The bey was henceforth required to give up all his powers over foreign affairs, defence and administrative reform to the French resident-general.

7e932bea-47e5-5386-9498-0e48388f3e95.name: Fountain
7e932bea-47e5-5386-9498-0e48388f3e95.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
7e932bea-47e5-5386-9498-0e48388f3e95.description2: Water fountains such as these were common in Ottoman government buildings in Lebanon, and were turned on whenever there was a meeting to prevent outsiders overhearing or eavesdropping. This marble fountain is octagonal in shape and is decorated with embossed semi-cylinders on each side. The exterior of the structure is decorated with a mosaic of black, white, beige and brown marble organised in geometric designs. A second, circular level of the fountain rests on this first octagonal structure.

802c443d-9ccb-5e7b-b692-21b1695a778f.name: Traditional suitcase
802c443d-9ccb-5e7b-b692-21b1695a778f.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
802c443d-9ccb-5e7b-b692-21b1695a778f.description2: Bags such as these were used by young brides, particularly in the 19th century, in order to transport their belongings to the marital home. As per tradition, the bag is made of black fabric and embroidered with the words *ma sha Allah* in Arabic calligraphy, meaning "as God wills". The words are embroidered in golden silk thread and surrounded by floral patterns.

81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.name: The Consuls’ Square [Alexandria, Egypt] after the Fire
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.author: Giulia Barrera
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.second_name: The ruins of the Consuls' Square in Alexandria (Egypt) after the bombing of the city by the British Navy in 1882
81a863b7-0e26-5e2a-b1ac-55b331836571.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.name: Mohamed Bey Mosque
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.history: Built in the late 18th century, this mosque is also known as the Sidi Mehrez mosque, probably due to its location facing the mausoleum to the saint Sidi Mehrez in the Bab Souika quarter. It is the only multiple-domed mosque in Tunisia. With clear Turkish influences, this mosque is reminiscent of the Hagia Sofia in Istanbul and the Pêcherie in Algiers.
8341e914-3245-5e20-9233-8addfbd06386.description2: The mosque is accessible through three doors, the most important of which opens up onto the *suq*, on one of the medina's most important streets. When seen from the outside, the mosque dominates the city, with its grouped domes and cupolas painted with a white wash. The Anatolian ceramic tiles covering the walls were an innovative addition at the time. The square-based prayer room is bordered on three sides by galleries, which each face onto three V-shaped courtyards. These galleries rest on marble columns with Turkish-style capitals. The richly decorated *mihrab* is covered in Iznik ceramic tiles. This mosque, also known as the Sidi Mahrez Mosque, is notable for being the only mosque in Tunisia with Turkish influences.

8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.name: The Emigrants
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.author: Marina Minozzi
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.keywords: Migration; Italian migration; Italian painters; painting; realism; artistic exchanges; Courbet; Macchiaioli; unification of Italy; social history; social topics; Italian society; post-unitarian Italian society; Livorno
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.copyright: Copyright image: Soprintendenza alla Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea.
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.description2: Angelo Tommasi is a naturalistic painter, influenced by Courbet’s realism, and he played an active role spreading the technique employed by the Macchiaioli. The monumental painting *The Emigrants* shows a common situation in Italy after the unification process. The dramatic theme of overseas emigration is vividly depicted by the packed crowds at the Port of Livorno, of people who have resigned themselves to their fate and the expectation of embarkation. The painting's extraordinary dimensions contribute to an illustration of the theme of Italian emigration on an almost epic scale.
8416e828-5b8b-5b06-93d0-9f518e17c49a.holding_institution_org: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM)

841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.name: Arab coffee pot
841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.author: Huda Kilani
841ba735-7c60-5603-8827-b02f6aedad8e.description2: One padded handle with leather, tapered cover; long covered nozzle, stamped reliefs. Coffee-drinking in a communal setting is an essential part of traditions in Bedouin communities to celebrate or mourn. This object of common use reflects the Bedouins’ traditions and everyday life and illustrates the variegated population composition of the Jordanian territory in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.name: The Court Martial at the Palace of Justice
84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.author: Giulia Barrera
84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.second_name: The military court set up by British authorities in Alexandria (Egypt) in 1882
84e87029-cd5f-539a-b16a-a7fedf6f4c7f.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city in ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.name: *Bashi Bazouk*
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
84f5327f-428b-5355-b4b7-9d4e62a12ef9.description2: This colourful watercolour, executed by the Istanbul-based, Maltese painter V. A. Preziosi, shows a Bashi Bazouk, a member of the irregular forces of the Ottoman army that came into use in the late 18th century. The bashi bazouk were mercenaries of great ethnic diversity, often from the Balkans, who fought for the Ottomans in hope of plunder, as they were not paid. An attempt by Husrev Pasha in Egypt to disband his Albanian bashi bazouks in favor of his regular forces began the rioting which led to the establishment of Muhammad Ali's rule. The bashi bazouk did not wear regular uniforms. In this case, the flamboyant character depicted here with his formidable moustache wears an astonishing array of clothing: a towering turban with tassles, an embroidered shirt and waistcoat with large open sleeves, a voluminous waistband and trousers. The outfit is finished off by elaborate footwear. A large yatagan dagger is secured in the waistband across the soldier's front, a gun slung across his chest.

86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.name: Small earthenware jar
86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
86c2720a-384b-58d3-92a2-3fc1aefd7f1c.description2: This double-handled and oval-shaped *qolla* has a long neck and a bulging lip. The decoration is polychromatic and organised in rows. On vase's belly, a row of medallions filled with flowers are bordered by a lattice strip and a herringbone strip on either side. The neck is decorated with alternating yellow, blue and green vertical lines. This item shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.name: *Napoléon II's journey to Algeria, 7 June 1865*
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.keywords: Diplomacy; Algeria; France; colonies; Napoléon III
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.second_name: Taken from *Histoire de l'Algérie et Voyage de Napoléon III en 1865. Photographies entre 1857 et 1867*
87367afd-5729-556e-a43a-bec2611cfa83.description2: Napoléon III visited Algeria twice during his reign (in 1860 and 1865). It was unusual at this time for the French head of state to travel outside the country, so these visits attracted much attention. They also allowed Napoléon to show how important Algeria was to him. He wanted to judge the complex situation which had been described to him in various reports for himself. A lavish welcome was prepared for him wherever he went during both his visits. This image, for example, shows an arc de triomphe which was erected in his honour at the terminus of a small mining train at Bouhamza.

874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.name: Institut Pasteur
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.history: l'Institut Pasteur de Tunis, created in 1893 by the nephew of Louis Pasteur, Adrien Loir, was the third Institut Pasteur in the world after Paris and Hanoi (now Ho-Chi-Minh City), and one of the 32 Institut Pasteur centres scattered around the world. The institute aims to provide a pioneering health service in the field of prevention, prophylaxis and cutting-edge research. Its prestige can also be attributed to the doctor Charles Nicolle, who was the director between 1903 and 1936 and discovered the typhus virus during his time there. l'Institut Pasteur played a decisive role in the fight against certain illnesses, such as rabies. It remains today an important national and international reference centre for many illnesses.
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.keywords: Charles Nicolle; Institut Pasteur; Nobel prize
874efcbf-3d66-55db-9523-6302edc55a76.description2: Initially a rabies vaccine centre, this building then became a general vaccination centre and finally an analysis laboratory. It is located at the crossroads named Place Pasteur, not far from the old European quarter, and eventually expanded from three, to nine, to eighteen laboratories. One of its biggest missions was concerned with diagnosis and public health, another with the production of vaccines and serums, and a third concentrated on research, development and innovation. The research clinic matched patients to clinical trials and worked in coordination with the various different laboratories and research teams.

884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.name: A Tunisian decoration (on the right) and an Italian decoration (on the left) awarded to a member of the Moreno family
884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.author: Massimo Sanacore
884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.archival: ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 17
884d9ccd-97ec-51c8-aec6-d384ad59224c.description2:
Two members of the Moreno family, Raffaello (Tunis 1844-1913) and his brother Leone (Tunis, 1852-1940) were awarded honours both by the Italian King (Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia) and by the Bey of Tunis (Nichan Iftikhar). The Morenos were Jews from Livorno (Italy), who had migrated to Tunisia in the early 19th century.  
Other Italians migrants in Tunisia were awarded both the title of Cavaliere dell’Ordine della Corona d’Italia by the Italian King and the title of Nichan Iftikhar by the Bey of Tunis, including Giuseppe Di Vittorio (a Sicilian who ran a construction company) and Luigi Rey (born in Tunis to an immigrant family from a village north of Turin, Piedmont, Italy, who also ran a construction company) and the Jewish Doctor Giacomo Castelnuovo.

8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.name: Letter from Father Joseph Yazbek to the Maronite Patriarch Yuhanna el-Hajj
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
8a101d28-6d11-5832-8d73-47c11308f989.description2: A small but growing Maronite community settled in the Chinatown area of Boston in the 1890s. In 1893, the Archbishop of Boston, John Williams, assigned F. Gabriel Korkemaz as the first Maronite priest. He was succeeded by his cousin, F. Stephan Korkemaz, two years later, and shortly afterwards by F. Joseph Yazbek. At the time, the hundred-or-so families that formed Boston's Maronite community worshiped at the St. James' Church on Harrison Avenue. Father Yazbek later bought a four-storey building on Tyler Street, which he remodelled to include a chapel, social hall, and priest's residence. This letter is a copy of a letter sent by Father Yazbek to the Maronite Patriarch Yuhanna el-Hajj, inviting him to the ceremony dedicating the Syro-Maronite chapel to Our Lady of the Cedars of Lebanon.

8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.name: Book cover
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.holder: Musée des Arts Islamiques de Kairouan
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.provenance: La zaouia de Sidi Sahbi, Kairouan
8a11b8a8-3b2f-5ba0-8118-5ec32059a75d.description2: This book cover from Rabat is decorated with a red and gold moulded pattern. The central medallion contains various florets, with two teardrops in a similar pattern emanating from it. The rectangular borders are made of a geometric interlaced pattern, whereas the four concave corners are surrounded by a curved border and floral motifs. This cover is evidence of the influence of the Ottoman school on Tunisian book covers.

8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.name: *James Robertson and His Brother-in-Law Felice Beato in Turkish Costume*
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.author: Bahattin Öztuncay
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.keywords: self-portrait; watercolour on photographs; Felice Beato
8ad123be-79dd-59a7-84a8-ffc0f7c6d8e7.description2: A self-portrait of James Robertson and his brother-in-law Felice Beato standing side by side and dressed in Turkish costume is an important work in the history of photography. This picture is in every sense a coloured counterpart of two other portrait photographs by Robertson first brought to light by Bahattin Öztuncay in 1991. The image of Felice Beato in this identical photograph is the only known picture of him in his youth.

8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.name: Cannon
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.type: Military object; firearms; arms and armour; artillery
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Cast steel; Arms; armour; Wood; Carriage; Cannon
8b7e80b3-625e-596c-a8d5-9f93e1bdc94b.description2: This small cannon on wheels was used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. This cannon is an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. The cannon is made of cast steel, with the chase, reinforce and cascable forged as one single part. It has two trunnions, used to mount the cannon on its carriage, a wooden body which is hollowed in the middle to make space for the cannon can pivot. It rest on a wooden cylinder and is linked by two wooden wheels.

8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.name: *Le général Khaireddine* (painting)
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.holder: Musée d’Histoire Moderne et Contemporaine de Kassar Saïd
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.keywords: Oil on canvas; Simil; General Khayr al-Din
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.materials: Canvas, wood, coloured pigments, gold leaf
8c7b0235-6bb9-503d-ac59-f73f7984f36b.description2: This 1852 oil on canvas by Simil depicts the General Khaireddine (Khayr al-Din) on horseback in official uniform. This brigadier-general uniform from the latter half of the 19th century comprises a full suit, a short coat, a shirt, a checia, a chemla and a pair of shoes. The brigadier-general also wore two crossed capes and a sword, with the Nichan al-Iftikhar (1st class) medal on the right-hand side of the chest, next to the insignas, and the Légion d'Honneur and the Ordre des Saints Maurice et Lazare medals on the left-hand side.

8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.name: Circular letter by the Italian Director General of Police to all the Italian Prefects, regarding 'Italian migration to Tunis and Bona (Algeria)'
8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.author: Anna Maria Iozzia
8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.archival: ASCt, Questura di Catania, el 4, b. 1, c. 76r
8c914730-20a7-5718-b92c-20ee629a7048.description2: The Italian consuls reported large numbers of unemployed Italian migrants in Bona (Algeria), where many Italians ended up begging in the streets, and in Tunis, where many Italians were in dire straits. The Director General of Police instructed the Prefects to inform the Italian population about this situation and warn it against “the shameful and fraudulent enticement by Migration Agents who, out of greed, push our peasants towards the most heartbreaking poverty”. The Prefects were also instructed to “assiduously prevent clandestine migration and repress its promoters”.

8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.name: *Muhammad 'Ali Pasha*
8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite
8f10719a-7586-5524-9036-a47811acc887.description2: Muhammad 'Ali Pasha, founder of Modern Egypt and Wali of Egypt in 1805. He was the head of the Alawiyya Dynasty that ruled Egypt from 1805 to 1952, and founder of modern Egypt. He came to Egypt in 1799 as part of a military unit to fight with the Turks – and the help of the British – to drive the French out of Egypt. However, the Turkish forces were defeated in 1799 in the Battle of Abu Qir.

8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.name: Little Sicily
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
8f933cf6-939e-5018-be2c-726c4f9ca78a.description2: Pictured here is an area, near the port of Tunis, where many immigrants from southern Italy had settled. Between 1865 and 1900, hundreds of small one or two-bedroom houses were built in the lower part of the Avenue Jules Ferry (today Avenue Habib-Bouguiba). The layout of the port allowed for the a rapid increase in the number of residents; a great many (mostly Sicilian) workers settled around the warehouses and workshops. Little Sicily therefore became both the home of the European working classes and the centre of the city's industrial activity. As Gaston Loth described it in 1905, "It's still Sicily, the children live in the streets, speak Arabic but also French, it's a like a swarm of lewd, barely dressed sparrows."

90bb7321-dadf-559d-862c-6d2c919236d2.name: Disembarking captives at La Goulette Port, Tunis.
90bb7321-dadf-559d-862c-6d2c919236d2.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
90bb7321-dadf-559d-862c-6d2c919236d2.description2: This document attests to the disembarkment of cargo and captives, abducted in the Mediterranean, at the La Goulette port, Tunis.

9226b1df-56b3-5ffb-a38d-64b0ff5cec56.name: African slaves working the fields
9226b1df-56b3-5ffb-a38d-64b0ff5cec56.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
9226b1df-56b3-5ffb-a38d-64b0ff5cec56.description2: This series of photographs attests to the existence of African slaves working in domestic roles or in agricultural labour.

92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.name: Palais de la Rose
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.history: The Palais de la Rose was built in the late 18th century, within La Manouba's royal gardens. Although originally used as a recreational palace for the Husainid beys, it soon began to receive many famous guests or persons visiting Tunisia, such as Queen Caroline of Brunswick in 1816. During the reign of Ahmed Pacha Bey (1837–1855) the palace became a residence for foreign teachers at the École Militaire du Bardo, among whom was the famous hero of Italian independence, Giuseppe Garibaldi. From 1881, the beginning of the French protectorate in Tunisia, the palace became the occupying army's headquarters. Following independence, the palace was restored and thus regained its original splendour and the became home to the Musée Militaire National.
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
92b5f36b-5cba-54c2-8f14-3426b9111ac4.description2: The Palais de la Rose is an example of "Moorish" architecture from Spain and North Africa with Italian influences. Its most notable features are the grand staircase, the great hall surrounded by a marble gallery, and the huge, luxurious courtrooms. It is richly decorated in a variety of styles, with Italian marble in rare colours and an elegant rococo style, as can be seen from the Neapolitan faience pottery, the vaulted ceilings, and the tympanums finely carved from stucco or naqsh hadida in one of the styles popular at the time, such as an eight-point star between two stylised cypress trees. Finally, palace-museum's four great rooms invite its visitors to learn about the history of the Tunisian army from antiquity to the War of Independence.
