92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.name: Photograph of Krste Petkov Misirkov with his friends
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.third_name: Fotografija na Krste Petkov Misirkov so prijatelite
92f613dc-01ad-5171-a5dd-b251dab90f70.description2: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) is the author of the book “On Macedonian Matters”, which was published in Sofia in 1903. This work is a starting point in explaining Macedonian distinctiveness, having served as an intellectual and contemplative engine for generations of Macedonians fighting in the battlefield and in literature alike.

933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.name: Dar Hussein
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.history: Built in the 12th century in the heart of the Banu Khorasan's royal city, this palace was occupied by the nobles of various dynasties who had ruled Ifriqiya. It became the seat of Tunis Municipality in 1858, after being restored and redecorated. The palace is named after the General Hussein, who was president of the municipality’s highest council. From 1882 until independence the palace served as the headquarters for the troops of the French occupation. It then became the seat first of Institut National d’Archéologie et Art, and in 1993 of l'Institut National du Patrimoine.
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; carved wood; painting
933220c7-ac0f-58a4-bd26-9a2aaf27779a.description2: Dar Hussein, one of the most beautiful palaces of the Tunis medina, shows traces of all the different eras of Tunisian architecture, from the Khorasani era through the Andalusian, Turkish and colonial eras.  On the ground floor, four large rooms, including a great hall, surround a peristyle. The neo-corinthian capitals topping the columns were made by Italian sculptors. On the first floor there is an elegant second peristyle in a 19th century Italian style, The galleries are divided up into four apartments, decorated with frescoes painted on faience pottery beneath a frieze of carved plaster.

94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.name: Migration preparations of Muslim families to Turkey
94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
94bc8ed7-7428-5a36-9919-9335c90547df.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.

96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.name: Necklace for horses – Type 2
96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewells; Precious stones; Beads
96a9d112-f072-5e5d-87c6-cce26768e6de.description2: This necklace was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of alternating silver spheres and amber cubic beads, with a silver cylindrical pendant in the centre.

97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.name: Wedding dress
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.author: Huda Kilani
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.materials: Linen with silk; hand weaving, hand embroidered, natural dyes
97603dc7-78b0-567d-995d-706683438f46.description2: The main fabric of this wedding dress is linen with silk selvedge stripes, with red and yellow taffeta inserts in the sleeves and skirt; the chest panel is couched with gilt cord and yellow, green and purple silk cord, and filled with multi-coloured stain and herringbone stitches. Palestinian weavers used manual spindles to prepare the cotton and linen threads imported from Egypt. Ashkelon weavers used light vertical hand looms (*Majdalawi* looms) to produce linen fabrics, while silk fabrics were spindled, died and woven in Syria. The Jordanian economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries relied on trade and crafts; new waves of people started to come to Jordan to participate in those industries. This object shows the diverse population composition of Jordan at that time, through personal attire, fashion, local costumes and rites.

9a102fc6-396b-58a9-ba31-7edc20e68a04.name: Report on the behaviour of Rustam Pasha
9a102fc6-396b-58a9-ba31-7edc20e68a04.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
9a102fc6-396b-58a9-ba31-7edc20e68a04.description2: A report on Rustem Pasha, the *mutasarrif* or governor of Mount Lebanon, and his treatment of his subjects. The report describes him as a tyrannical and unjust governor with oppressive policies, curbing the autonomy of tribunals, for example. He also imposed high taxes on the tobacco trade in Mount Lebanon and ignored many of the Sultan's decrees.

9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.name: Gold to the country from the [Italian] colony in Tunisia
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.author: Massimo Sanacore
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.archival: ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 13
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.second_name: Receipt for the donation of gold to Italy, in support of its war effort during World War I
9a2d1d61-3abf-5d45-a7c7-9550d4cd751a.description2:
This receipt certified that Leone Moreno (Tunis, 1852-1940) “donated gold to the country” in order to support Italy’s war effort during WWI. Leone was the grandchild of Mosè Moreno, a Jew from Livorno who migrated to Tunis around 1830. In Tunisia, the Morenos became successful in business. Leone’s father and brothers were traders and bankers, while Leone was an agricultural entrepreneur.  
He was a nationalist and was one of the Italians who actively resisted the French policy of assimilating the Italians in Tunisia. He employed only Italian workers on his estate and supported the Società Dante Alighieri, a society aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad. Leone Moreno also generously supported the Italian hospital Giuseppe Garibaldi and the Italian orphanage “Principe di Piemonte”.

9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.name: *View of Istanbul*
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
9b44e7da-e4ce-51fe-a09e-946b4f817954.description2: Felix Ziem, who incorporated the seasons and the changing light of the sun during the day into Venetian scenes, selected Istanbul – another city intertwined with the sea – as a subject for this particular work. Portraying a quiet village at the shores of the Bosporus and the boats on the sea, the painting is dominated by the golden colour of sunset. Ziem is deemed a particularly successful artist in terms of capturing the reflections of sunlight on the water. Recognizing this feature as Ziem’s forte, Theophile Gautier mentions the effects of the changing light of the sun – as part of the movement in the environment – reflecting on the water as “broken into a thousand fractions”. As in his other works, the figures have been transformed into a few colour stains in the picturesque atmosphere.

9b806efe-99d1-5b6e-913c-0ee466605547.name: Letter from l’Institut d’Afrique in Paris, congratulating Ahmed Bey for having abolished the slave trade
9b806efe-99d1-5b6e-913c-0ee466605547.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
9b806efe-99d1-5b6e-913c-0ee466605547.description2: This letter from August 1841 from l'Institut d'Afrique in Paris, signed by both its president and general secretary, congratulates Ahmed Bey for having abolished the slave trade in his kingdom, and awarding the Tunisian Prince a *diplôme de protecteur*.

9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.name: A battle between Algerian ships and ships of the Naples Royal Navy, which chased the Algerian ships and ultimately destroyed them by firing cannon shots on 17 May 1792
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.author: Rossana Spadaccini, Giulia Barrera
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.archival: AS NA, Segreteria di stato di azienda, Piante, 35
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.third_name: *Espressione di una caccia intrapresa a due Sciabecchi Algerini dalla Fragata di Sua Maestà Napoletana denominata Sirena, a dì 17 maggio 1792, nelle acque comprese fra le isole d’Jeres ed il Capo Tagliato, quale termina per distruggerli e sommergerli a colpi di Cannone nella spiaggia denominata Cavallara*
9c275ab6-ba7e-5a89-909a-fd6b396dc11b.description2: In the 18th century the Kingdom of Naples and the Regency of Algiers were among the countries that competed for the control of trading routes in the Mediterranean and that participated in privateering. Only in 1856, by the Declaration of Paris, did Great Britain and most of other major European countries (with the exception of Spain) declare privateering illegal. By the time, Algeria had already become a French colony. The French military occupation of Algeria had in fact started in 1830.

9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.name: Newspaper *al-Wataniyya*
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
9cf0fa7d-8af1-5fb8-bd4a-1b1c8b14129b.description2: This issue of *al-Wataniyya*, only part of which is shown here, dates to 1 February 1901. *Al-Wataniyya* was a bi-monthly newspaper founded by N. A. Mokarzel and written, edited and printed in Philadelphia, USA. It was distributed internationally.

9cfc95e2-dcd3-56fd-b37e-253ac1e09a34.name: *Immigrants* \[on Ellis Island\]. *Two Italian kids*
9cfc95e2-dcd3-56fd-b37e-253ac1e09a34.description2: At the start of the 20th century millions of Italian families emigrated to America by boat, driven by economic misery and the hope of a better life. Once they arrived, the immigrants were taken to have a number of checks done by the Ellis Island authorities, as they had to satisfy certain standards (hygiene, health) or risk being repatriated. One can understand, therefore, why these two well-dressed Italian children seem anxious.

9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.name: The Students’ Benevolent Fund of the Società Dante Alighieri
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.author: Giulia Barrera
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 122
9dbfd8cd-e3bf-5f5f-bd09-c7f5a2634953.description2: The Dante Alighieri Society – created in Italy in 1889 and still in existence ‒ is aimed at promoting Italian language and culture abroad; its Tunisian branch was established in 1893. In Tunisia the Dante Alighieri Society devoted its energies into promoting schooling and supporting school attendance. One should consider, in this regard, that the Italian community at the time was composed of workers, miners, and labourers and included several destitute members. The students’ benevolent fund of the Società Dante Alighieri (Patronato scolastico) was created in 1898 and was aimed at supporting school attendance of destitute children, by providing free books and clothes.

en: Pendola, M., *Gli italiani di Tunisia: storia di una comunità (XIX-XX secolo)*, Foligno: Editoriale Umbra, 2007.

9e555530-36a5-59e9-a179-0f1bdff61fd4.name: Seated *Pifferari*
9e555530-36a5-59e9-a179-0f1bdff61fd4.description2: The first significant waves of Italian migration abroad began in the mid-19th century during a period of great economic difficulty, with most migrants travelling to neighbouring European countries. One example of this was the "pifferari" - Italian shepherds from Abruzzo or Calabria who sung traditional songs accompanied by pipes - who started arriving in Paris. The famous French artist Charles Nègre (1820–1880) often focussed his work on street scenes such as this one.

9f97dfd5-8a30-53f7-9503-d00f973c94b8.name: Jacket
9f97dfd5-8a30-53f7-9503-d00f973c94b8.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
9f97dfd5-8a30-53f7-9503-d00f973c94b8.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's formal jacket, which he wore for his welcome ceremony in exile. It is made of pure black wool with floral patterns embroidered in golden thread.

a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.name: Sahib el-Tabaa Mosque
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.history: This mosque was the last great work of the Husainid dynasty of Tunisia. It was built by the powerful Youssef Saheb el-Tabaa between 1808 and 1814. Being the richest man in the country during Hammouda Pacha Bey's reign, he used his wealth to set up a variety of activities around his mosque, such as two madrasas and the tomb of its founder, similar to the Turkish Konya. The décor and ornamentation reflect Western influences, with a narrow and elegant minaret.
a10695d2-fbb1-56b0-aaa5-5b25ce6071ac.description2: This mosque's imposing height dominates the Place Halfaouine. The layout of the mosque is organised around its main prayer room, which is composed of nine naves and seven bays. The barrel-vaulted ceiling is covered in stucco, and decorated with vegetative and floral motifs and with geometric elements, such as stripes and stars, reflecting both its Italian and Turkish influences. It is also boasts of having the only five-domed prayer room in the city. The walls are covered in marble panels imported from Carrara (Italy) and ceramic tiles from Qallaline. The thin tall columns are ribbed and topped with composite capitals. The *mihrab*'s polychromatic decoration is mixed with the pseudo-gothic arches and floral motifs. The Sahib el-Tabaaa mosque is noteable for being one of the clearest examples of the Italian influences on religious architecture.

a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.name: *A Mamluk Resting with his Horse*
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.description: The Mamluks were excellent horsemen and aroused the attention of artists like Carle Vernet and Sebastian of Bourbon, a member of the Spanish Royal family. Artists did not need to have journeyed to the Near East or Arabia to be labelled Orientalists. This is a good example, because the authors did not travel to the Near East.
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.author: Carmen Linés Viñuales
a34c17e6-990c-5cb0-95c0-c85297eb94e1.artist: Original: Carle Vernet; copyist and lithographer: Sebastián María Gabriel Borbón y Braganza

a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.name: List of 15 'Tunisian Turks' captured by corsair captain Giuseppe Diano from the Kingdom of Sicily and sold in Palermo
a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.author: Renata De Simone
a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.archival: ASPa, Consultore del Governo, Tribunale delle prede, vol. 264, carte senza numerazione
a3577379-4a3e-5997-913a-756fad78ca88.description2: The documents explain that the captain corsair Giuseppe Diano plundered a Tunisian galliot and captured 15 “Tunisian Turks”. The captives’ names and ages (ranging from 15 to 55 years old) are listed. The document further explain that three out of such 15 captives had been sold to private individuals, while the remaining 12 had been bought by the Commissioner of the Committee for the Redemption of Captives (Deputazione della redenzione de’ cattivi); inferring that they were to be exchanged for Italian captives held in Tunisia. The Committee for the Redemption of Captives’ mission, in fact, was to negotiate the liberation of the subjects from the Kingdom of Sicily held as slaves.

a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.name: *Inside a Jewish household*
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.archival: Tunis au XIXe Siècle: Aquarelles et Textes de Charles Lallemand, Apollonia, 2001.
a4ee987f-15bb-56a1-b262-8f402df53ad9.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour by Charles Lallemand shows the inside of a bourgeois Jewish household. This snapshot of daily life reveals a great deal of similarity between Jewish and Muslim traditional dress and interiors.

a5b9fc7a-39f3-548a-ab66-613df1cdc6e7.name: Pendant for horses – Type 1
a5b9fc7a-39f3-548a-ab66-613df1cdc6e7.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
a5b9fc7a-39f3-548a-ab66-613df1cdc6e7.description2: This pendant was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. It is made of a single, lozenge-shaped silver plaque decorated with red coral and blue gemstones. Silver leaf-shaped pendants dangle from this plaque and produce a tinkling noise when moving, announcing the arrival of the rider.

a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.name: *The Grand Bazaar*
a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
a5c93080-d37b-5926-ad79-2d9bb61932f2.description2: Amadeo Preziosi often presented genre scenes from Istanbul in his unique style. Specifically, he incorporated diverse scenes from the Bazaar in a number of his paintings. This venue, particular to Istanbul, has been of great interest to western artists, and in Edmondo De Amicis’s words “is not just a building but a town”. The Grand Bazaar, which housed shops for a wide range of commercial goods and catered to almost all of the needs of customers, offered an incredible visual richness and diversity to the western artist. A reflection of this opulence is also evident in Preziosi’s painting, which includes numerous details from daily life.

a6c96df7-d704-593e-8558-88a1905ae818.name: Musée d’Enfidha
a6c96df7-d704-593e-8558-88a1905ae818.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
a6c96df7-d704-593e-8558-88a1905ae818.history: From the first, this monument was built as both a church and a museum for Tunisia's ancient Christian art. Built in a neo-Roman style in the centre of Enfidha by European colonisers, this old church was consecrated to Saint Augustine, the patron saint of Roman Africa, on 1 May 1907. In 1964 the building, which had ceased to function as a church, was turned into a regional archaeological museum.
a6c96df7-d704-593e-8558-88a1905ae818.keywords: Architecture; Romano-Byzanine style; vaults; stained-glass windows; tapestry; marble
a6c96df7-d704-593e-8558-88a1905ae818.description2: The building, whose entrance sits underneath a clock tower, is built in the shape of a Latin cross, with an apse at the end where the choir can be found. The numerous important discoveries in the region in 1901 and 1905 encouraged the directors, the Archbishop of Carthage and the Société Franco-Africaine d’Enfidha to decorate the walls of the cathedral with an impressive series of Christian mosaics, all with a funerary or martyrologic theme. The museum houses an important collection of ancient ceramics. A number of pagan funerary or votive steles from local archaeological sites can also be found in the museum.

a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.name: Khayr al-Din Pacha
a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.author: Bechir Yazidi
a7c102ce-f4bb-5330-8383-c17696408f62.description2: Khayr al-Din Pacha brought in many reforms which significantly changed the precolonial period, to a great extent Westernizing the Beylik of Tunis, which was later portrayed as "modernization". This Mamluk of circasian origin was probably born in 1825, and came to Tunis as a child in 1840. He quickly climbed the ranks and took his father-in-law Mustapha Khaznadar's place as Chief Minister under the rule of Mohamed Sadok Bey from 1873 to 1877. He died in 1890 in Istanbul, where he had served as grand vizier. He appears tall and majestic in this photograph, and carries authority in his piercing gaze. His jacket is richly decorated, bearing the coat of arms of the sovereign who bought him and brought him to Tunis, Ahmed Bey (1835–1855).

a7fd98fa-f450-5ba3-b6d2-3909a56326ac.name: Decorated panel featuring a mosque
a7fd98fa-f450-5ba3-b6d2-3909a56326ac.description2: An Ottoman-style mosque, identifiable by its cone-shaped minarets, sits in the middle of this horseshoe arch supported by two columns. The lower panel contains a vase with various flowers emerging from it, such as carnations, tulips, and vine leaves. A dense rinceau pattern with flowers and leaves fills the gaps in the arch and the keystone and decorates the capitals of the columns. The main colours are yellow green and blue, although beige and brown also feature. This item shows traces of both Ottoman and Andalusian influences.

a9281dfb-f5ce-5f06-9747-94bf00a2f99e.name: Shield
a9281dfb-f5ce-5f06-9747-94bf00a2f99e.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
a9281dfb-f5ce-5f06-9747-94bf00a2f99e.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Cast steel; Arms and armour; Shield
a9281dfb-f5ce-5f06-9747-94bf00a2f99e.description2: These shields were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. This shield is an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. It was used mainly by foot soldiers, and was hand-held with straps going around the wearer's arm. Although ineffective against newer weaponry such as guns, the shield was used by soldiers to deflect arrows or swords. It is made of cast steel, with no decorative elements of notes. It features four bosses and reverse arm fixings.

a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.name: The cutting of granite blocks for the construction of the first dam on the Nile. Many Italian stonecutters participated in the works
a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.author: Patrizia Pampana
a946e99a-c0f3-5d45-9fb0-6eec1cfb9b75.description2: In the year 1900, Count Giulio d’Aspremont (an Italian diplomat), visited the construction site of the first dam across the Nile (today known as the Aswan Low Dam or Old Aswan Dam). He took several photographs of the works and of the monuments on the island of Philae that were slate to be submerged by the water. He published some of them on the *Bulletin of the Italian Geographical Society*, where he wrote that up to 2,000 Italian workers were employed in the works (as stone-cutters, miners and masons), out of a total labour force of about 10,000 or 12,000; an Italian village had sprung up on the Nile banks, with modest little houses, trattorias and shops.

a95aa12b-08ad-5216-93c1-8009226cdb57.name: Saint-Cyprien. Combine harvesters and sheaf binders on the road.
a95aa12b-08ad-5216-93c1-8009226cdb57.second_name: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
a95aa12b-08ad-5216-93c1-8009226cdb57.description2: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This is a photograph from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate the land. It shows two combine harvesters which had been imported for the development of intensive cereal faming, and would have been used as advertising for Europeans considering investing in this type of agricultural "company".

abac828d-5728-5fdb-8767-366c5beb8fa5.name: Café du Marabout in the Souk Ettrouk
abac828d-5728-5fdb-8767-366c5beb8fa5.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
abac828d-5728-5fdb-8767-366c5beb8fa5.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
abac828d-5728-5fdb-8767-366c5beb8fa5.archival: Copied from a drawing by Sir Grenville Temple, published in his book The Shores and Islands of the Mediterranean in London in 1840, this drawing was taken from Chelli Zouhir, La Tunisie au Rythme des Estampes du Xve au XIXe siecle (Tunis, ed. Tunis Carthage: 1992), p. 65, fig. 25.
abac828d-5728-5fdb-8767-366c5beb8fa5.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book Tunis et ses Environs shows the Café el-Mourabit in the Turkish souk, also known as the tailors' souk, in the Tunis medina near the Zaytuna Mosque. The café was especially known for its Andalusian architecture. The customers sit on mats sipping coffee, leaning on archways and pillars.

ae85f44d-6a24-58d0-81d8-1e9715c81ac8.name: Colonial style building
ae85f44d-6a24-58d0-81d8-1e9715c81ac8.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
ae85f44d-6a24-58d0-81d8-1e9715c81ac8.history: In Tunis, the capital of the Protectorate imposed by France on Tunisia in 1881, the European quarter built itself right next to the old Arab medina. A new kind of home - the investment property - soon appeared, and the term balas (from the Italian *palazzo*) became widespread. These two or three-storey housing blocks greatly affected the city's urban landscape by introducing many different architectural styles as well as new architects, designers and builders with from different backgrounds. The 19th century was the century of eclecticism in Tunisia (both neo-classical and neo-baroque), whereas the 20th century was most marked by the influence of Art Nouveau.
ae85f44d-6a24-58d0-81d8-1e9715c81ac8.keywords: Art Nouveau; colonial style; eclecticism; Neo-Baroque
ae85f44d-6a24-58d0-81d8-1e9715c81ac8.description2: 114 Rue de Yougoslavie, the former French Embassy and General Residence previously known as the Disegni building, was designed by the famous architect Auguste Peters, who remains a leading figure of eclecticism. The finely carved balconies, ribbed stone corbels, delicate Venetian style mouldings, overhanging arches and columned galleries all add to the building's majestic character. Auguste Peters was a great master of eclecticism in the first decade of the 20th century, and decorative elements like these characterise his work.

aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.name: Bowl with stand
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.holder: Musée de la Céramique Sidi Kacem Jelizi
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.keywords: Floral motifs; winged motifs; cermaics from Nabeul
aed162cf-cef3-52e5-aa78-567138f64d2a.description2: This bowl with a bulging rim sits on a stand. The decoration is made of two layers of concentric patterns around a central circle, filled with winged motifs. These green and brown patterns are painted on a yellow background. Although this kind of bowl is usually used to serve couscous, in the town Nabeul, and particularly for the occasion of Islamic New Year, each child is presented with a *methred* bowl, filled with golden couscous, dried fruit, dates, a hard-boiled egg and sweets. This all surrounds a statuette made of sugar, moulded and coloured to resemble an animal (such as a rooster or a gazelle) or a figure, like a doll or cavalier.

afd9edc1-f5ea-5e44-91d3-f71b09a91a1e.name: *Ibrahim Pasha*
afd9edc1-f5ea-5e44-91d3-f71b09a91a1e.keywords: Ruling Family; Rulers of Egypt; The Alawiyya Dynasty; Turks; The Ruling Elite
afd9edc1-f5ea-5e44-91d3-f71b09a91a1e.description2: Second ruler of the Muhammad 'Ali Dynasty, Ibrahim Pasha was the oldest of Muhammad 'Ali Pasha’s sons and his right hand in his conquests and projects. He came to Egypt with his brother Ahmad Tusun in 28 August 1805. He ruled Egypt for only two months.

b1189adf-8651-54d6-9426-8461bdc5c6a6.name: Figurine of a dog
b1189adf-8651-54d6-9426-8461bdc5c6a6.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
b1189adf-8651-54d6-9426-8461bdc5c6a6.description2: Dimitrija Chupovski (1878–1940) was the President of the Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society in St. Petersburg also known as St. Petersburg Colony of Macedonians. Chupovski was also actively engaged in publishing of the periodical Macedonian and Russian-language publication, “Makedonski Golos” (“Macedonian Voice"), first issued in 1912.

b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.name: A treaty between the Regency of Tunis and the Grand Duke of Tuscany, concerning the jurisdiction over Tuscan Jews who migrated to Tunisia
b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.author: Loredana Maccabruni
b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.archival: ASFi, Trattati Internazionali, CXCII [192]: “Modificazione del Trattato commerciale fatto colla Reggenza di Tunisi nel 1822 relativamente agli Israeliti”
b3139452-a18c-5578-a8f9-65f5a88d9fe0.description2:
Treaty of one article, in Italian and Arabic, signed by the Tuscan Consul Enrico Nyssen and by the Bey Ahmed Bascià, sealed with a wax seal of the Consulate General of Tuscany, and ratified by the Grand Duke of Tuscany Leopold the II on 29 January 1847.  
This treaty modified the 1822 treaty between the two countries which had given to the Jews from Livorno the same status of Tunisian Jews (placing them under the Beys' jurisdiction). According to this new treaty, the Tuscan Jews who had moved to Tunisia (or would move to Tunisia in the future) and registered in the Tuscan Consulate, were placed under Tuscan jurisdiction and protection. Such provision did not apply to the so-called “Grana” Jews who had moved to Tunisia from Livorno (Tuscany) in the late 17th century.

b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.name: *Djouni. The residence of Lady Hester Stanhope*
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.keywords: Joun; Lebanon; women; Romanticism; travel; traveller; drawing
b5036b5d-8c8a-54bc-9e98-cd2351f8ef63.description2: William Henry Bartlett was a prolific topographical artist who travelled extensively in search of new and interesting subjects for his drawings. He visited North Africa and the Middle East seven times and made several other trips in Britain and Europe, as well as North America. Popular demand for travel books was high during the 1830s and 1840s and Bartlett contributed illustrations to several of them including about a dozen written by himself. His aim as he described it was 'to give lively impressions of actual sights'. Bartlett visited the celebrated Lady Hester Stanhope, a British adventurer and traveller, at her residence in Joun in the Lebanon in June or July of 1834 and produced this watercolour during his visit.

b5822b19-0bac-505f-bb0c-be6490cc1dc6.name: List of the Christian captives of Italian origin, written by Mariano Stinca, a Neapolitan captive
b5822b19-0bac-505f-bb0c-be6490cc1dc6.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
b5822b19-0bac-505f-bb0c-be6490cc1dc6.description2: This list of the Chrsitian captives of Italian origin (Calabria Crotone, Catanzaro, Borgia, Palermo, etc.) was written by Mariano Stinca, a former Neapolitan captive who had become the secretary and head of protocol for Hammouda Pacha Bey.

b891c040-ed12-5331-bbcb-c0107a795fd7.name: Letter from the British residents of Gibraltar, congratulating Ahmed Bey for having closed the slave markets
b891c040-ed12-5331-bbcb-c0107a795fd7.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
b891c040-ed12-5331-bbcb-c0107a795fd7.third_name: *A testimonial of gratitude to His Highness the Bashaw Bey of Tunis for his philantrophic and most noble resolution to abolish the inhuman and horrible traffic in Slaves…*
b891c040-ed12-5331-bbcb-c0107a795fd7.description2: This letter signed by approximately 30 British residents of Gibraltar, congratulates Ahmed Bey for having abolished the slave trade and closed the slave markets in the Tunisian regency.

ba1c6502-ece8-50c7-a051-8ccb55d13f84.name: Letter from the Tunisian merchants of Egypt to the Bey of Tunis
ba1c6502-ece8-50c7-a051-8ccb55d13f84.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
ba1c6502-ece8-50c7-a051-8ccb55d13f84.description2: This letter from the Tunisian merchants of Egypt to the Bey of Tunis thanks him for nominating a new representative in Alexandria. The letter is signed by over one hundred merchants in both Cairo and Alexandria

bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.name: *The European neighbourhood of Tunis and the Northern Suburbs*
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.author: Patrizia Pampana
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.third_name: *Quartiere europeo e sobborgo di Sugga, parte settentrionale di Tunisi*
bb7e5c73-80d2-53d1-8bb0-be2895feb51b.description2: An early photograph of a view of Tunis, the picture shows in the European neighbourbood. It was taken on a trip to Tunisia organised by the Italian Geographical Society (Società geografica italiana) in 1875.

bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.name: Newspaper *al-Hawi*
bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.holder: House of the Maronite Patriarchate of Antioch and all the East
bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
bc06907f-aa68-5c8f-a06c-e1664310cd2a.description2: This issue of *al-Hawi* dates t 13 April 1914. *Al-Hawi* was a weekly literary, political and comic periodical founded in August 1912 by José M. Shaia and written, edited and printed in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.name: Italian police record of Romualdo Peppini (b. Turin 1863, d. Casablanca 1912), an Italian anarchist worker who immigrated to Morocco in 1901
bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.author: Giulia Barrera
bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.archival: Ministero dell’interno, Direzione generale di pubblica sicurezza, Divisione affari generali e riservati, Casellario politico centrale, b. 3725, f. “PAPPINI, Romualdo”
bca9a195-0769-5794-865b-e5e0b784277a.description2: In the 19th century and for the first half of the 20th century political migration streamed from Italy to North Africa. Supporters of Italian unification, and especially the supporters of Republican nationalist ideologue Giuseppe Mazzini, were among the first migrants. After the Italian unification, some anarchists migrated, while under Fascism several antifascists took refuge in North Africa.

bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.name: Villa Maria, in Tunis, the mansion of Luigi Rey, the son of a migrant from Piedmont (Italy)
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.dates: Photograph: first years of the 20th century; building: late 19th century
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.author: Giulia Barrera
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 44
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.third_name: *Villa Maria del cav. Luigi Rey, imprenditore*
bd591c95-bb06-5105-b1bd-b95187ad7a88.description2: Luigi Rey was the son of Italian immigrants Giuseppe Rey (1808-1897), of Piedmont and Adelaide Baldacci, of Tuscany. In 1836, Giuseppe Rey was dispatched to Tunis by his employer, a construction company from Genoa, to work in the Bardo Palace (the official residence of the Bey of Tunis). After completing the contract Giuseppe decided to stay in Tunisia, where he continued to work at the service of the Bey. Together with his three children (Luigi, Antonio and Pio), Giuseppe Rey set up a construction company that continued after his death. Predominantly with his brothers but at times on his own, Luigi Rey built a variety of private and public edifices, including the Tunisia Palace Hotel (designed by architect Resplandy).

en: Finzi, Silvia (ed.), *Architectures italiennes de Tunisie/Architetture italiane di Tunisia*, Tunis: Finzi/Ambasciata d'Italia, 2002.

bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.name: Jeweller’s tools box
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.holder: Jordan Folklore Museum, Department of Antiquities
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.author: Huda Kilani
bd9ac0b4-17dd-5d2a-86a5-baadbae9f621.description2: Jeweller’s wooden box to keep tools such as hand drills, punctures and screws, and soldering iron clumps. This tool box belonged to an Armenian jeweller whose family left their country during the First World War and settled in Jerusalem. The jeweller then moved to Amman and settled there in 1948. The Armenians were well known as skilled craftsmen and jewellers. The owner of this box worked as a jeweller since the 1950's, using his tool box until his death. The tool box demonstrates the relationship between different waves of migration and the variegated demographic composition of the Jordanians.

bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.name: The stand of the Italian Community in Tunisia at the International Exhibition held in Turin in 1911
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.author: Massimo Sanacore, Giulia Barrera
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.archival: ASLi, Archivio Moreno di Tunisi, b. 15
bdc77deb-d803-5076-89a4-a826a7e730aa.description2:
The picture shows how, on the occasion of the 1911 international exhibition in Turin the Italian community in Tunisia chose to represent itself by blending elements taken from the Italian and from the Tunisian material culture.  
One can read the sign E. & A. Coen, Tunisi, Susa, Sfax. Eugenio and Alfredo Coen were the owners of a furniture factory and of the imposing furniture shop, “Au Palais Arabe”, in downtown Tunis.

bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.name: Hôpital Habib-Thameur
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.history: This hospital, built in 1891 in the el-Halfaouine quarter by a group of Italian doctors, was initially called l'Hôpital Colonial Italien de Tunis and served the Italian residents of the city, most of which had emigrated from Sicily. It was moved to the building of the current Hôpital Habib-Thameur on the 15 March 1900, and in 1907 was renamed l'Hôpital Giuseppe Garibaldi, after the famous hero of Italian independence. Upon the arrival of English troops on 7 January 1943 it became a French hospital, and was renamed again to l'Hôpital de la Libération on the 6 June of the following year. It was finally given its current name by the Tunisian government following independence, in honour of the great doctor and militant nationalist Habib Thameur.
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.keywords: Hospital; Charles Nicolle; Giuseppe Garibaldi; Habib Thameur
bde2bde2-7481-545c-9b6c-11a32b97be4d.description2: This hospital, which was constantly being expanded and renovated, started off with 150 beds. The hospital was served by Italian doctors, who were quickly joined by French doctors, and provided general medical services, as well as surgery, internal medicine, ophthalmology and radiology. Like the Hôpital Charles Nicolle, it also became prestigious university hospital following Tunisian independence.

be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.name: Dawud Pasha’s bedroom
be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
be8c9494-f659-53be-b44a-b763609d1e3d.description2: This bedroom belonged to the first *mutasarrif* (ruler) of the Mount Lebanon *mutasarrifiyya*, Dawud Pasha, who governed from 1861–68). The room is furnished with one double bed, one baldachin bed, two curtains, one rug, two embroidery panels, two bedside tables and a coffer. A thin off-white mattress covered in silk and embroidered in gold thread rests on each bed, and both frames are covered with light blue silk draperies. Three small, rectangular off-white silk pillows rest against the baldachin bed's adjustable headboard. Two square pillows rest on the double bed. The blue silk drapery on the bed frames was also used for the identical silk curtains. The curtains served a purely decorative function and could not be closed, as they were sewn to the valances, which are made with off-white silk and gold embroidery. The curtains are held back with golden tiebacks hooked on golden metal knobs. The embroidery panels on the walls are also made with the same off-white silk, and feature a variety of floral designs. The two dark, wooden bedside tables resemble classical columns and the coffer is made with a lighter wood and decorated with floral bas-reliefs.

bf34096f-295d-5f0d-931b-71a243d32a5b.name: Sofa of Krste Petkov Misirkov
bf34096f-295d-5f0d-931b-71a243d32a5b.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
bf34096f-295d-5f0d-931b-71a243d32a5b.description2: Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) is among the most prominent personages of the recent Macedonian history. He was highly educated philologist, historian, ethnographer and publicist, having also been engaged in translation. He lived and worked in St. Petersburg, Russia. Besides his most important work "On Macedonian Matters", he had around thirty articles published in different newspapers.

c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.name: An Italian booklet printed in Tunis in 1898 by Socialist and Anarchist Typography on the trial against the Italian anarchist leader Enrico Malatesta
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.author: Giulia Barrera
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.archival: *Una pagina di storia del partito socialista-anarchico: resoconto del processo Malatesta e c.ni*, Tunisi: Tipografia socialista-anarchica, 1898
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.description2:
Enrico Malatesta (1853-1932) was one of the most important Italian anarchist leaders and theorists. He spent a good part of his life in exile in different countries (including Argentina, Egypt, France, Lebanon, Siria, England and the United States). In 1882, he went to Egypt to support the revolt of Ahmad Urabi and was arrested by British authorities. In 1897, he was living in Ancona, in Central Italy, when he was arrested and put on trial. After serving seven months in prison, he was placed in internal exile on the island of Lampedusa (south of Sicily) from where, in 1899, he fled to Tunisia, then to Malta, then on to England.  
Italians in Tunisia set up a number of associations, political groups, newspapers, and cultural institutions of different political persuasions.
c0647b9c-1ac0-53b5-a15b-d5505d2f8137.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

c120b65a-cd13-5c60-a28b-463b99dc6f57.name: Three
c120b65a-cd13-5c60-a28b-463b99dc6f57.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
c120b65a-cd13-5c60-a28b-463b99dc6f57.description2: These water pipes, or *araghil* (sing. *arghile*), is made of translucent glass painted with floral patterns in pale colours. The *araghil* have three main parts: first, you have a bowl for the coals sitting on top of a metal plate. Under this is the body of the *arghile*, which can come in a variety of shapes and sizes, and consists of a gasket and water jar. Connected to the main body is a pipe for smoking. The *arghile* originated in Persia and later became popular in 17th century Turkey, used by the Ottoman elite as a status symbol. The water pipe became hugely popular, and in 1841 even sparked a diplomatic crisis between France and the Ottoman Empire. However, although it remains popular in the modern Middle East, it was largely replaced by cigarettes in the 20th century. The *arghile* woks by vaporizing a flavoured tobacco called *shisha*, which is passed through water and then inhaled. Depending on their placement, the coals can either be used to boil the water and thus create water vapour, or to produce smoke by burning the tobacco. These *araghil* were used by Ottoman officials in 19th century Lebanon.

c2b61064-ccd9-5fe4-8725-750d1cb45ef7.name: Architectural drawing of Mar Mikhael train station
c2b61064-ccd9-5fe4-8725-750d1cb45ef7.author: Jeff El-Msanne, Julien El Khoury
c2b61064-ccd9-5fe4-8725-750d1cb45ef7.description2: This architectural drawing shows the plan of the Mar Mikhael (Saint Michael) train station that was built in 1891. The station served as a terminal for visitors to the city, and was in use until 1976.

c2b70678-bfae-5de0-a210-547e266d7099.name: Emigrant family
c2b70678-bfae-5de0-a210-547e266d7099.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
c2b70678-bfae-5de0-a210-547e266d7099.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. This photograph belongs to the Luka Likidis family, who migrated from Bodrum to Crete in 1916.

c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.name: *Caiques and Sailboats at the Bosporus*
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c2d7dded-69f6-5450-9ae1-d5680237968b.description2: Felix Ziem was able to produce works in many styles such as portraits, still life, genre scenes and historical depictions, though he is primarily renowned as a landscape artist. He was an active member of the Barbizon school, which primarily focused on the depiction of nature. In the painting, Istanbul is represented through a few mosque silhouettes in the background. Nonetheless, as in his Venetian scenes, the painting emphasizes the picturesque union of the city, the sea and human figures, which have been reduced to mere colour stains. Ziem, who produced his own paints from natural pigments, influenced other artists with the use of colour in his paintings. He is known to have used “lapis lazuli” for the dominant blue colour in this painting.

c4f3ee34-3e55-5cf6-ab02-eee9f50cdc11.name: *Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939)*
c4f3ee34-3e55-5cf6-ab02-eee9f50cdc11.keywords: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro; Jugoslavia; Vienna; Austria
c4f3ee34-3e55-5cf6-ab02-eee9f50cdc11.description2: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939) as a child. Danilo was the eldest son of King Nicola I of Montenegro. He was married to Princess Jutta von Mecklenburg-Strelitz and had to leave Montenegro after it was integrated in the kingdom of Yugoslavia after WWI. He died in 1937 in Vienna, Austria – in exile.

c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.name: *Encampment of the Awlad Said Mount Sinai 1839*
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.author: Ulrike Al-Khamis
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.description2: The Awlad Said are a large clan of the Sawalha tribe, traditionally based on Southern Sinai. It was escorts from this tribe that accompanied Roberts during his traversing of the Sinai. This depiction gives a detailed impression of their traditional encampments and tent construction. Situated in a valley sheltered by high, rugged mountain ranges, the encampment consists of severalrows of low, rectangular tent structures with flat roofs. Separating walls and screens within are created by striped, woven textile units. Inhabitants of the camp are seen seated in small groups, engaged in conversation or standing in groups, lances in hand. The men are dressed in headscarfs, gowns and cloaks of varying colour, while the few female figures that appear are cloaked in black abayas, all-enveloping black cloaks. From a ravine in the far background, a long caravan of men and camels approaches the camp.
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.artist_birthplace: David Roberts: Edinburgh, Scotland; Louis Hague: Tournai, Belgium
c5af0628-6524-5b0d-a3ae-ef6099a54a96.artist_deathplace: David Roberts: London; Louis Hague: London

c5b30d17-788f-5526-9443-d7a3c584472b.name: Italian peasants in Tunisia
c5b30d17-788f-5526-9443-d7a3c584472b.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 24
c5b30d17-788f-5526-9443-d7a3c584472b.description2: According to official statistics, in 1921 there were around 4,000 Italian peasants in Tunisia; together with their families they amounted to 15,400 people, or roughly 60 per cent of the Europeans employed in agriculture.

en: Cresti, F., “Prefazione”, in Daniela Melfa, *Migrando a Sud. Contadini italiani in Tunisia (1881–1939)*, Rome: Aracne, 2008: 19.

c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.name: *Top of the garden at Marengo, ancient Marabout*
c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.author: Dalila Orfali
c869c0fc-13da-5c97-9a34-aeb4470de17e.description2: This part of Algiers has a particularly rich history. The painting depicts the famous mausoleum of Sidi Abderrahmane Ettaâlibi ('Abd al-Rahman al-Thalibi) who was a member of one of the most ancient families of Algiers. He was buried here in the 7th century and was made the Patron Saint of Algiers due to his reputation as a wise and knowledgeable man.

c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.name: *View of Istanbul*
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.archival: Orientalist Paintings Collection-Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Collection
c96923cb-dba0-5c95-81e1-1742fdb0a515.description2: This particular Istanbul painting by Felix Ziem reveals the picturesque aspect of life at sea against the backdrop of the city’s silhouette. The composition of the sailboats and marines in the foreground is balanced by the cityscape with a monumental mosque structure in the background. The artist’s use of vibrant colours and his efforts to capture the shimmering effects of the constant change of light with a fast, dynamic brush stroke technique dominate the painting. This style has led Ziem to be compared with impressionist painters, and even to be regarded as an artist who foreshadowed the emergence of impressionism with his work. The use of brilliant sunlight, which is considered as the major contribution of orientalist painting to European art is evident in the city's cap in the background.

ca6bd475-805d-5b06-a1e3-16bb93242b3b.name: *The interior of the Queen's carriage: meeting between Louis-Philippe and Queen Victoria*
ca6bd475-805d-5b06-a1e3-16bb93242b3b.artist: Lithographer: Jules David; artist: Édouard Pingret
ca6bd475-805d-5b06-a1e3-16bb93242b3b.description2: Keen on keeping up good relations with the United Kingdom, King Louis-Philippe of France accepted Queen Victoria's invitation in 1844. Accompanied by Guizot and his youngest son, the Duke of Montpensier, he was received lavishly by the English royal family. In 1842, Queen Victoria became the first sovereign to take the train between London and Windsor. Since then, British rail companies had begun setting up carriages especially reserved for the Royal Family. One of the key experiences offered to Louis-Philippe was the opportunity to travel by train in one of these spectacular carriages.

cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.name: Hôtel Majestic
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.history: This was the first luxury or grand hotel in Tunis. Built in 1912 and designed by the architect Paul Baron in an Art Nouveau style, in the early 20th century the Hôtel Majestic was the best hotel around. It was requisitioned by the German army between November 1942 and May 1943 and became the seat first of the Kommanduntur, then, after liberation, of the American army headquarters. After Tunisian independence and until the mid sixties President Habib Bourguiba used the hotel to receive many foreign heads of states and official guests. Many famous foreign artists, such as Brasser, Barbara, Aznavour, Luis Marino and Bécaud, who had come to Tunisia to give concerts or recitals, also stayed in the Hôtel Majestic.
cafcd6e4-6930-5d23-8538-b552e0f9216e.description2: Located on Avenue de Paris, the Hôtel Majestic offered, from a decorative and structural point of view, something totally new. With its sunny façade and terrace, this four-storey building was the first of its kind in the city. The furniture, woodwork, lighting and the rooms, which opened out onto one another in a modern fashion, were what gave the hotel its charm.

cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.name: Tourbet el Bey
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.history: The Tourbet El Bey monument is Tunisia's largest and most famous royal mausoleum from Ottoman or Husainid times, notable for its architecture and exterior, as well as for its size and number of cupolas and tombs. It was built by 'Ali Pacha Bey II, the fourth bey of the Hussainid dynasty, around 1770. A *kouttab*, a *sabil*, and a large *madrasa* were also founded in association with this mausoleum. This necropolis for the Beys of Tunis holds the tombs of the Husainids and their families, as well as those of a few important members of the nobility or loyal servants and ministers.
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; necropolis
cb50db24-36a3-5378-b0e6-e03a650cef9b.description2:
This funerary complex, composed of eight spacious rooms, is set around two courtyards, one surrounded by porticos and another open-air. The rooms and patios contain the tombs of 165 different beys who had governed Tunis from 1759 to 1942. The room for the ruling beys is notable for by its Arab-style cupolas, similar to those in the Sidi Mahrez Mosque.  
A second room is covered by a barrel vault - unique to Tunisia - decorated with wonderfully carved stuccos. The walls, on the other hand, are decorated in an Italian style with slabs of coloured stone or marble marquetery. The rooms are all decorated with faience ceramics, which are evidence of this necropolis' European and Arab influences as they were both imported from Europe and locally produced. This monument-cum-museum houses one of the most important collections of funerary inscriptions.

cbdc629e-10f9-51ce-82d1-89858dea84f0.name: Munchar - arrival of the post
cbdc629e-10f9-51ce-82d1-89858dea84f0.second_name: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
cbdc629e-10f9-51ce-82d1-89858dea84f0.description2: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This is a photograph from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate it. Pictured is a local driver bringing the mail van to the immigrant communities in Munchar (in the Béja region.) This picture was taken to reassure prospective immigrants that they would be able to easily communicate with their families back home.

cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.name: The English Consulate (Ruins)
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.author: Giulia Barrera
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.second_name: The ruins of the English Consulate in Alexandria (Egypt) after the bombing of the city by the British Navy in 1882
cbffe8c2-7457-5662-8cc7-208d2edc343c.description2:
The author of this picture, Luigi Fiorillo, was an Italian photographer who migrated to Alexandria (Egypt) around 1870 and opened a successful photography shop. In 1877, he participated as photographer in an expedition to Shewa region (Ethiopia), organised by the Italian Geographical Society, and ten years later in an Italian military expedition for the colonial conquest of Eritrea.  
In 1882, Fiorillo was one of the few Europeans who remained in Alexandria after the anti-foreign rioting and documented the consequences of the British bombardment on Alexandria of July 11th. He collected 50 pictures of the city ruins in an album titled “Souvenir d'Alexandrie: Ruines, 1882”.  
On the back of some photos that he took in the 1880s, Fiorillo defines himself as “le photographe de Son Altesse le Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha” (the photographer of his Majesty Prince Mohammed Toussoun Pasha). Luigi Fiorillo died in 1898.

en: Silingardi, Adriano, ”Luigi Fiorillo, l’avventuroso fotografo di Alessandria d’Egitto”, unpublished paper (available on line) for the exhibition of the same name, Genoa, 2014.

cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.name: General Giuseppe Garibaldi, hero of the Italian national unification, arriving in Tunis in 1834
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.holder: State Library of Modern and Contemporary History
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.author: Giulia Barrera
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.archival: *Storia illustrata della vita di G. Garibaldi* per Antonio Balbiani
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.description2:
In 1833, Giuseppe Garibaldi (1807-1882) joined Mazzini’s organization, Giovane Italia, a republican group that supported the unification of Italy, and in 1834 he participated in an attempted insurrection. He was sentenced to death by the Kingdom of Sardinia and fled abroad. He spent time in Tunis in the first half of 1835.  
Later, Garibaldi went to South America (1835-1848) where he fought for the independence of different countries. When he came back to Italy he fought to defend the Roman Republic (1849), and in 1860 led a successful expedition of one thousand volunteers in Southern Italy to defeat the Kingdom of Two Sicilies and unify it with Central and Northern Italy.  
During the Italian Risorgimento, several other liberals and supporters of Italian unification were forced to go into exile. Several went to North Africa.
cf6fd523-ce44-5925-8fcb-a5eba1bea0a5.holding_institution_org: Biblioteca di Storia Moderna e Contemporanea

cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.name: Colonial farms
cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.history: French colonialism brought significant changes to Tunisians' lifestyles, which consequently affected the country's rural architecture. The colonial settlers built their homes as soon as they arrived, and so Italian and French residential architecture evolved from a small hut to a large house. These old, often large, farmhouses punctuate the landscape with their red roofs and cellars, easily distinguishable against the green of the forest. They remind us that the great Italo-French rivalry was triggered by the competition over the best land, as viticulture was their main economic activity. Single-crop farming was used for these grapevines, which were almost entirely wine varieties.
cfc8881a-67a2-5e47-b165-244089d5800d.description2: This farmhouse, belonging to the French winemaker of Grombalia, can be distinguished by its white walls and industrial red tiles, stamped to show the name of their maker and place of origin. The tiles are overlapping to protect the house from the rainfall and snowfall. Contrary to the traditional farmhouses which were inward facing, this settler farmhouse has large windows on its façade and is built on a empty plot of land. The house is east facing and rectangular-based, with four annexes dedicated to the farm's needs, most importantly pressing the grapes and storing them in the cellars.

cff9d211-aedd-5f72-abe6-63319cd03d80.name: Photograph of Krste Petkov Misirkov
cff9d211-aedd-5f72-abe6-63319cd03d80.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
cff9d211-aedd-5f72-abe6-63319cd03d80.keywords: Scientific literary society; standardisation of language
cff9d211-aedd-5f72-abe6-63319cd03d80.description2: Krste Misirkov (1874–1926) was a grandiose and profoundly nationally designated personage of the 19th century. He lived in St. Petersburg and was an esteemed and highly engaged member of the Slav-Macedonian Scientific Literary Society. He contributed to the standardization of the modern Macedonian language, having given responses to some important issues of the history, culture and language of Macedonians.

d0827146-e2b8-5b30-8059-2505a64042be.name: *The arrival of the refugees*
d0827146-e2b8-5b30-8059-2505a64042be.author: Maria Dimitriadou
d0827146-e2b8-5b30-8059-2505a64042be.description2:
The arrival of Greek refugees in Thrace 1922. Photographer unknown.  
The “Convention concerning the exchange of Greek and Turkish population" was signed at Lausanne, on 30 January 1923, by the two governments. It involved approximately 2 million people (around 1.5 million Anatolian and 500,000 Muslims in Greece), most of whom were forcibly made refugees.

d08f212c-1246-5ca4-a5cb-8f7562d35936.name: Farmers and sharecroppers at Munchar with their families
d08f212c-1246-5ca4-a5cb-8f7562d35936.second_name: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
d08f212c-1246-5ca4-a5cb-8f7562d35936.description2: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This photograph shows an example from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate the land. The number of people in this photograph - many of whom are pitifully dressed - shows us that those employed were often large families, searching for work in an attempt to escape the poverty of their home countries.

d35ea140-6436-50e0-a3c8-f37c54eabc12.name: Jacket
d35ea140-6436-50e0-a3c8-f37c54eabc12.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d35ea140-6436-50e0-a3c8-f37c54eabc12.description2: Yusuf Bey Karam's formal jacket, which he wore during his youth. It is made of red velvet with floral patterns embroidered in gilded thread.

d389d855-8b86-5926-9175-35f1c9a7b75b.name: Vambrace
d389d855-8b86-5926-9175-35f1c9a7b75b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d389d855-8b86-5926-9175-35f1c9a7b75b.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Cast steel; Arms and armour
d389d855-8b86-5926-9175-35f1c9a7b75b.description2: Dawud Pasha's vambrace. Made of cast steel, this vambrace contains two hollowed circles with engraved floral patterns.

d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.name: Pair of pistols
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.type: Military object; metalwork; firearms; arms and armour
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.keywords: Military object; Metalwork; Steel; Arms and armour; Pistol; Silver
d4f7349c-29d1-5924-babf-a4c0256713a9.description2: These Turkish pistols were used by the Ottoman soldiers in Lebanon in the 19th century to quash resistance movements. As the Lebanese resistance had no weapons of their own, the fighters frequently ambushed Ottoman soldiers and took their weapons. These pistols are an example of such weaponry, which was taken by the resistance and used against the Ottomans. They are silver decorated miquelet-lock pistols with bulbous butt plates. They are made of wood and cast steel.

d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.name: Jewellery for horses – Type 2
d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels; Precious stones
d4f761e5-39cf-5040-a028-277cc5dd0f2b.description2: This pendant was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. It is made of a single, lozenge-shaped silver plaque decorated with turquoise, burgundy and blue gemstones. Short, thin silver chains with leaf-shaped pendants dangle from this plaque and produce a tinkling noise when moving, announcing the arrival of the rider.

d5ef573d-2a05-5d47-a3e9-ad45caf58169.name: Flag of the St Petersburg Colony of Macedonians
d5ef573d-2a05-5d47-a3e9-ad45caf58169.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
d5ef573d-2a05-5d47-a3e9-ad45caf58169.description2: This flag was the symbol of the St. Petersburg Colony of Macedonians, a group of Macedonian intellectuals who lived and worked in St. Petersburg and shared the same ideas and interests – working for the liberation and recognition of Macedonia. The red colour of the flag symbolizes the blood shed in the centuries-long Macedonian struggle for autonomy. The white rectangle in the upper left corner bears a depiction of a unicorn, also in red colour.

d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.name: In Tunis, the families of the Italian men drafted for the war waiting to get their daily allowance from the Italian government
d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.author: Massimo Sanacore, Giulia Barrera
d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.archival: *La colonia italiana di Tunisi durante la guerra 1915-1917*, Tunisi, 1917. ASLi, Famiglia Moreno di Tunisi, b. 8.
d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.third_name: *Sussidi governativi. Il pagamento del soccorso giornaliero alle famiglie dei richiamati*
d6cffdd2-cbd5-5bf7-bd67-0a2b5084a2cc.description2: According to a booklet published in 1917 by the Tunisian branch of the Dante Alighieri Society and quoted by historian Adriano Salmieri (see his contribution to the volume *Mestieri e professioni degli italiani di Tunisia* – *Métiers et professions des Italiens de Tunisie, a cura di S. Finzi, Tunisi: Finzi*, 2003), by the end of April 1917 11,146 Italians in Tunisia had been drafted for the war, and 700 had died. According to the same source, in 1917 in Tunisia the Italian government was paying daily allowances to almost 5,000 destitute families of drafted soldiers.

en: Finzi, Silvia (ed.), *Mestieri e professioni degli italiani di Tunisia/Métiers et professions des Italiens de Tunisie*, Tunis: Ambasciata d'Italia, Istituto di cultura, 2003.

d72b69f9-a4da-50e3-9f8d-3294ff84d9e9.name: The 1861 constitution
d72b69f9-a4da-50e3-9f8d-3294ff84d9e9.author: Bechir Yazidi
d72b69f9-a4da-50e3-9f8d-3294ff84d9e9.description2: Despite the promulgation of the fundamental pact, the new reforms did not, in practice, take effect. The French and English consuls therefore continued to remind the Tunisian sovereign of the importance of judiciary reform in particular and offered to create a senate to assist him in this. Mohamed Bey's successor, Sadok Bey, promised to complete his predecessor's work and create a deliberative assembly. On 1 July 1860, the completion of the new reforms was announced. On 17 September 1860 in Algiers, the bey solemnly handed Napoléon III a copy of the richly bound text. Proclaimed in January 1861, the constitution was put to effect the following 23 April.

d9c388f4-ae74-56f2-b3d4-341eda234a0f.name: Panel with a large bouquet
d9c388f4-ae74-56f2-b3d4-341eda234a0f.description2: This polychromatic panel is decorated with an image of a bowl filled with pears, apples and other fruits, topped by a small vase with flowers such as carnations, tulips, sunflowers and daisies coming out of it, which are interlaced with a rinceau pattern of palmettes, half-palmettes and vine leaves. The main colours are blue, green and brown. The decorative style, colour palette and manufacture all indicate a typical Tunisian ceramic, containing a mix of Andalusian and Ottoman influences.

da83b646-c418-524e-8eff-75e69c1f77d9.name: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939) and Princess Jutta of Mecklenburg-Strelitz
da83b646-c418-524e-8eff-75e69c1f77d9.keywords: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro; Jugoslavia; Vienna; Austria
da83b646-c418-524e-8eff-75e69c1f77d9.description2: Danilo I, Prince of Montenegro (1871–1939) with his wife, Princess Jutta von Mecklenburg-Strelitz. Danilo was the eldest son of King Nicola I of Montenegro. He was married to Princess Jutta von Mecklenburg-Strelitz and had to leave Montenegro after it was integrated in the kingdom of Yugoslavia after WWI. He died in 1937 in Vienna, Austria – in exile.

dd685f6f-e2d6-5e02-846e-ac9afcd7f6a4.name: Necklace for horses – Type 1
dd685f6f-e2d6-5e02-846e-ac9afcd7f6a4.author: Marie Therese Moujabber
dd685f6f-e2d6-5e02-846e-ac9afcd7f6a4.keywords: Decoration; Silver; Silver chains; Jewels; Precious stones; Necklace
dd685f6f-e2d6-5e02-846e-ac9afcd7f6a4.description2: This necklace was used on the horses of Ottoman officials and indicated their high status and wealth. The chain consists of fifteen silver squares with sawtooth framing, connected to a smaller rectangular silver piece and three dangling silver bells. The silver squares are decorated with red coral semi-precious gemstones arranged in a circular shape. The bells would make a tinkling noise and announce the arrival of the rider.

ddc859b5-2660-59d5-a43e-bea3692d92db.name: Italian stonecutters in Tunisia
ddc859b5-2660-59d5-a43e-bea3692d92db.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 25
ddc859b5-2660-59d5-a43e-bea3692d92db.description2: At the turn of the twentieth century, the Italian community in Tunisia included large numbers of masons, stonecutters, diggers and other manual workers. In this period, most of Italian migrants preferred to seek their fortunes in the Americas and in other European countries. Those who migrated to North Africa were only a small percentage, nonetheless they amounted to dozens of thousands.

ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.name: Dress
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.author: Huda Kilani
ddd75581-2e37-5baa-8483-63c54f368af5.description2: Long black silk dress (*malas*), narrow at the waist, wide at the bottom, embroidered with cross-stitch dark blue and red on the chest and on the front side, worn by women of the al-Druze tribes, with a shirt underneath. This object illustrates the variegated composition and the demographic changes of the Jordan population in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It also shows how the different populations brought with them their fashion, costumes and rites which contributed to the multifaceted social and cultural heritage of Jordan. The al-Druze tribes migrated from Syria (Hawran) to northeast Jordan in the early twentieth century because of their support for the Syrian revolution against the French occupation.

dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.name: Rababa
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.holder: Jordan Museum for Costumes and Jewellery, Department of Antiquities
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.author: Huda Kilani
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.keywords: goats gut; animals skin; horse hair
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.materials: Wood, animals skin; handmade and hand painted
dff63501-6388-5281-9baf-bb1a3d253e7f.description2: Four pieces of wood formed into a rectangular shape; the top and bottom are covered with animal skin and joined with goat’s intestines. The rababa is played with a bow consisting of an arched stick with horse hair. The rababa is a musical instrument widely used in the Bedouin tradition. Music played in communal setting is an essential part of the traditions in Bedouin communities for leisure at communal gatherings.

e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.name: Paul Draneht, his wife Adele Casati and their daughter Despina
e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.author: Massimiliano Cremona, Ignazio Galella
e055e6ed-ffba-5b33-a42a-7f9060dc3802.description2:
Paul Draneht (1815-1894) was born in Nicosia (Cyprus) as Pavlos Pavlidis. He was the child of a Greek Christian Orthodox family who fled Cyprus to escape the clashes between Greeks and Turks and then took refuge in Egypt.  
The Khedive of Egypt sent him to study in France. He later had a brilliant career in service to the Khedive participating in the negotiations on the opening of the Suez Canal. He became superintendent of the Egyptian Opera Theatre and commissioned the opera Aida to the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi.  
Paul Draneht married Adelaide Casati, the daughter of a cello player who performed at the Aida premiere. Their daughter Despina Draneht married a Greek businessman, Emmanuel Zervudachi.

e1f071ed-6026-5f1b-bac8-49caf60ecd7a.name: Migration preparations from Lemnos island to Turkey
e1f071ed-6026-5f1b-bac8-49caf60ecd7a.holder: Population Exchange Museum (The Foundation of Lausanne Treaty Emigrants)
e1f071ed-6026-5f1b-bac8-49caf60ecd7a.description2: The 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey was based upon religious identity, and involved the Greek Orthodox citizens of Turkey and the Muslim citizens of Greece. The "Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations" was signed at Lausanne, Switzerland, on 30 January 1923, by the governments of Greece and Turkey. During the migration waves during the 1896-97 riots in Crete, 40,000 Cretan Muslims had to migrate to territories under Ottoman rule: Lebanon, Syria and Anatolia. This photograph pertains to migration preparations from Lemnos to Turkey in 1924.

e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.name: A letter from the Hashemite court
e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.description: A letter from the Hashemite court signed by al-Hussein bin 'Ali, the king of Arab countries and Sharif of Mecca. The letter was sent to the princes Faisal and al-Aziz al-Jarba, from Umm al-Qura (Mecca) in Rajab, 18th, AH 1336 / AD 1917 asking them to take care of Jacobean Armenian confession and to help them and to protect them as they protect themselves, their fortune and their sons. It says also to facilitate what they need either in their stay or travel, because they are free non-Muslims enjoying Muslim protection. Those are people who prophet Muhammad makes his will to take care of, and the one who doesn’t do so will be his (Muhammad's) adversary till Judgment Day. King Hussein says: this is one of the most important orders we ask you to do. He ends his letter by praying to God to grant the Emirs to do what he asks them.
e24c667e-3e74-52ad-9357-51224ea2c3d0.author: Aida Naghawi

e25a6015-7ec0-5c37-9571-2555b21065b7.type: Object for personal use; walking help
e25a6015-7ec0-5c37-9571-2555b21065b7.author: Nada Andonovska (author), Dragan Georgiev, historian (consultant)
e25a6015-7ec0-5c37-9571-2555b21065b7.keywords: National issues; European League of Nations
e25a6015-7ec0-5c37-9571-2555b21065b7.description2: The book “On Macedonian Matters” by Krste Petkov Misirkov (1874–1926) provides the only comprehensive national program dealing with important national and political issues at the turn of the 20th century. The work of this great visionary and analyst was published for the purpose of drawing the attention of the European League of Nations to Macedonia, whose existence as separate nation was not recognized.

e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.name: Portrait of Hammouda Pacha Bey
e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.keywords: Oil on canvas; Hammouda Pacha Bey
e5c4e1fa-cda0-5a71-9b74-c7a6f465f4ad.description2: This oil on canvas is a portrait of Hammouda Pacha Bey before the dress code reform, in traditional dress with a cashmere shawl and dagger in his right hand. Hammouda Pacha Bey, nicknamed the builder of modern Tunisia, was a qualified and military man and was known as a firm but fair ruler.

e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.name: Slave market
e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.holder: Institut Supérieur d’Histoire Contemporaine de la Tunisie
e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e5e027ae-6390-53b1-82f7-668b99a7615c.description2: This souk, Souk el-Birka, was built by Youssef Dey in the early 17th century in the Tunis medina, and was used for the purpose of selling slaves. It was served, until the 16th century, by seasonal carriages from sub-Saharan Africa. By 1850, the number of slaves and their descendants in Tunisia was estimated to be around 80,000. The majority did agricultural work in the oases in the south, but many were also working in domestic roles in bourgeois households and the bey's residence. In 1841 Ahmed Bey banned the sale of slaves and demolished the stores reserved for this purpose, and in 1842 he abolished slavery.

e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.name: A book on the activities of the Italian community in Tunisia, published by the Italian Chamber of Commerce of Tunisia for the 1906 International Exhibition in Milan
e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.author: Giulia Barrera
e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906.
e696126e-a8d7-5829-87b8-1372eb83e64c.description2:
In 1906, in celebration of the Simplon Tunnel opening between Italy and Switzerland, the Italian government organised an international exhibition in Milan. On that occasion, Italian communities in Egypt and Tunisia published books that described their lives and activities.  
In Tunisia, Italians entrepreneurs and professionals set up a committee charged with organising the participation to the exhibition of the Italian community in Tunisia.

e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.name: Palais du Baron d’Erlanger
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.author: Saloua Khadhar Zangar
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.history: The history of this monument cannot be separated from its creator's personality. The rich Orientalist painter and Arabic musicologist Baron d'Erlanger moved to Sidi Bou Said in 1911, where he built is palace. He dedicated his life to the preservation of Tunisia's architectural, artistic and musical heritage, and on his death in 1932 was buried in Sidi Bou Said. Notable examples of his work are his vital efforts towards the preservation of Sidi Bou Said, and his remarkable seven-volume work on Arabic music.
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.keywords: Architecture; Andalusian style; Italian style; stucco; carved wood; painting
e6b08b1b-d850-518a-9f8a-7c3f457e761d.description2: This palace is built on a hill overlooking the sea, and covers approximately 3,300 m2, occupying just a small portion of the 5-hectare grounds. Built between 1912 and 1922, the palace is notable for its interesting architecture, inspired by Tunisian traditions with elements of Andalusian, Venetian and Arab ornamentation. Behind its huge sea-facing façade, it is organised into three distinct sections. The two main square patios, on two separate floors, are connected by galleries, and all surround a covered central space. The décor consists of wall decorations, ceramic panels, carved stucco panels, stucco carved ceilings, golden or painted carved wooden ceilings, and more.

e6b696c1-80fd-5fd5-8b33-a15b88ca3ccb.name: An Italian Pasta Factory in Tunisia
e6b696c1-80fd-5fd5-8b33-a15b88ca3ccb.author: Giulia Barrera
e6b696c1-80fd-5fd5-8b33-a15b88ca3ccb.archival: Comitato della Camera italiana di commercio ed arti, *Gli italiani in Tunisia*, Tunis, 1906, p. 36
e6b696c1-80fd-5fd5-8b33-a15b88ca3ccb.description2: According to historian Adriano Salmieri, in 1921 the four Tunisian towns of Tunis, Sfax, Sousse (Susa) and Bizerte had a total of 133 Italian shops making pasta and bread. Making pasta was hard work. In Tunisia, the industrialization of pasta production started only in the 20th century.

en: Finzi, Silvia (ed.), *Mestieri e professioni degli italiani di Tunisia/Métiers et professions des Italiens de Tunisie*, Tunis: Ambasciata d'Italia, Istituto di cultura, 2003.

e714183d-faa1-5c38-bf56-e05a8f41f61e.description2: This copy of a beautiful watercolour from Charles Lallemand's book *Tunis et ses Environs* shows the Porte de la Mer, or the Porte de France, around which both European settlers and Tunisian residents are gathered. Its location was strategic, as it led to both the Tunis medina and the European quarter.
